title.zh: 卷二百九十一 列傳第五十 吳育 宋綬 李若谷 王博文 王鬷
title.en: Volume 291 Biographies 50: Wu Yu, Song Shou, Li Ruogu, Wang Bowen, Wang Zong
title.raw: 卷二百九十一 列傳第五十 吳育 宋綬 李若谷 王博文 王鬷 Volume 291 Biographies 50: Wu Yu, Song Shou, Li Ruogu, Wang Bowen, Wang Zong

sentences.zh: 吳育，字春卿，建安人也。

translations.literal: Wu Yu, style name Chunqing, was a native of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu, courtesy name Chunqing, was a native of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 父待問，與楊億同州里，每造億，億厚禮之。

translations.literal: His father Daiwen was from the same prefecture and district as Yang Yi; whenever he visited Yi, Yi treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daiwen was a fellow townsman of Yang Yi. Whenever Daiwen called on him, Yi received him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 門下少年多易之，億曰：「彼他日所享，非若曹可望也。」

translations.literal: Many young men in [Yi's] entourage looked down on [Daiwen]. Yi said, "What that man will enjoy in days to come is not what you fellows can hope for."
translations.idiomatic: Many of the young men in Yi's household treated Daiwen lightly, but Yi said, "The honors that man will one day enjoy are not within your reach."

sentences.zh: 累官光祿卿，以禮部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: [Daiwen] rose through repeated offices to Grandee of Splendid Happiness and retired as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Daiwen rose through the ranks to Grandee of Splendid Happiness and retired as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 育少奇穎博學，舉進士，試禮部第一，中甲科。

translations.literal: Yu in youth was exceptionally bright and broadly learned. He passed the jinshi examination, ranked first in the Ministry of Rites trial, and was placed in the top class.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yu was unusually gifted and widely read. He took the jinshi degree, placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination, and was graded in the highest cohort.

sentences.zh: 除大理評事，遷寺丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Reviewing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed reviewing clerk in the Court of Judicial Review and later promoted to vice director of that court.

sentences.zh: 歷知臨安、諸暨、襄城三縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Lin'an, Zhuji, and Xiangcheng counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Lin'an, Zhuji, and Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 自秦悼王葬汝後，子孫從葬，皆出宦官典護，歲時上塚者，往來呼索擾州縣。

translations.literal: From the time Prince Daowang of Qin was buried in Ru onward, descendants buried with him were all overseen by eunuchs. Those who came each year to tend the tombs traveled about shouting demands and harassing prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Prince Daowang of Qin was interred in Ru, the collateral burials of his descendants had been managed by eunuchs, and the annual tomb visits brought envoys who shouted for supplies and harassed local governments along the route.

sentences.zh: 育在襄城，請凡官所須，具成數，毋容使者妄索，羊豕悉出大官，由是民省供費殆半。

translations.literal: When Yu was in Xiangcheng, he requested that all supplies required by officials be fixed in set amounts, that envoys not be allowed to demand at will, and that sheep and swine all be issued by the Court Provisioner. Thereby the people saved nearly half their supply costs.
translations.idiomatic: While magistrate of Xiangcheng, Yu required that every item owed to visiting officials be listed at fixed quantities, forbade envoys to levy arbitrary demands, and had all sheep and pigs supplied by the imperial kitchen. The people thereby cut their hospitality costs by nearly half.

sentences.zh: 宦官過者銜之，或中夜叩縣門，索牛駕車，育拒不應。

translations.literal: Eunuchs who passed through bore resentment toward him. Some knocked at the county gate in the middle of the night demanding oxen and carriages; Yu refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs who passed through nursed a grudge against him. Some would pound on the county gate at midnight demanding oxen and carts; Yu would not oblige them.

sentences.zh: 異時宗子所過，縱鷹犬暴民田，入襄城境，輒相戒約，毋敢縱者。

translations.literal: At other times when imperial clansmen passed through, they would let hawks and dogs ravage the people's fields. When they entered Xiangcheng's territory, they would warn one another by agreement not to let them loose.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere, when imperial clansmen traveled through they would loose hawks and hounds to trample the people's fields, but once they entered Xiangcheng they warned one another not to dare do so.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，擢著作郎、直集賢院、通判蘇州。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Worthy and Upright, promoted to Drafting Secretary, posted directly to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and made Vice Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as worthy and upright, he was promoted to drafting secretary, assigned to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and appointed vice prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 還知太常禮院，奏定禮文，名《太常新禮慶曆祀儀》。

translations.literal: He returned to direct the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Regulations, submitted fixed ritual texts, and titled them New Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Qingli Sacrificial Protocols.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to head the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Regulations, drafted revised ritual codes, and presented them under the title New Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Qingli Sacrificial Protocols.

sentences.zh: 改右正言，歷三司鹽鐵、戶部二判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrator and successively served as Controller of the Salt and Iron Commission and of the Revenue Commission within the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrator and served in turn as controller of the Salt and Iron Commission and of the Revenue Commission.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官供諫職。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he held his existing office while performing remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he retained his title while serving in a remonstrance capacity.

sentences.zh: 元昊僭號，議出兵討之。

translations.literal: Yuanhao usurped a royal title, and the court debated sending troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao assumed a royal title, the court debated dispatching an army against him.

sentences.zh: 群臣曰：「元昊，小醜也，旋即誅滅矣。」

translations.literal: The ministers said, "Yuanhao is a petty villain and will soon be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said, "Yuanhao is a petty rebel who will be wiped out in no time."

sentences.zh: 育獨建言：「元昊雖稱蕃臣，其尺賦斗租，不入縣官，且服叛不常，請置之，示不足責。

translations.literal: Yu alone submitted advice: "Although Yuanhao calls himself a vassal of the frontier, his taxes by the foot and grain by the peck do not enter the imperial treasury, and his submission and rebellion are inconstant. I ask that he be set aside and shown to be unworthy of being held accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Yu alone argued: "Though Yuanhao styles himself a frontier vassal, his levies never reach the imperial treasury, and his loyalty shifts with every season. Let him be ignored—show that he is beneath our reproach.

sentences.zh: 且已僭輿服，勢必不能自削，宜援國初江南故事，稍易其名，可以順拊而收之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, he has already usurped imperial carriages and robes and by force cannot reduce himself. It is fitting to follow the early-dynasty precedent of Jiangnan and slightly change his title, so that he may be soothed and brought in."
translations.idiomatic: He has already assumed forbidden regalia and will not willingly strip them away. We should follow the early-Song precedent used in Jiangnan—alter his title slightly so that he can be pacified and brought back into the fold."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not respond.

sentences.zh: 復上言：「宜先以文誥告諭之，尚不賓，姑嚴守禦，不足同中國叛臣亟加征討。

translations.literal: He submitted again: "It is fitting first to admonish him with written proclamations. If he still does not submit, for the time being hold the defenses strictly; he is not to be treated like a rebel within China and subjected at once to punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again: "Send written proclamations first. If he still refuses allegiance, tighten the defenses for now; there is no need to treat him like a domestic rebel and rush into a punitive war.

sentences.zh: 且征討者，貴在神速；

translations.literal: Moreover, in punitive campaigns speed is prized;
translations.idiomatic: Punitive campaigns depend on speed;

sentences.zh: 守禦者，利於持重。

translations.literal: in holding defenses, steadiness is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: defensive warfare profits from steadiness.

sentences.zh: 羌人剽悍多詐，出沒不時，我師乘銳，見小利小勝，必貪功輕進，往往墮賊計中。

translations.literal: The Qiang are fierce and full of stratagems, appearing and vanishing at no fixed time. Our army, riding its keen edge, seeing small gains and small victories, will surely crave merit and advance lightly, often falling into the enemy's schemes.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang are fierce and treacherous, striking when least expected. Our troops, flush with confidence, will chase petty gains and rush ahead—only to walk into their traps.

sentences.zh: 第嚴約束，明烽候，堅壁清野，以挫其鋒。」

translations.literal: Only tighten discipline, make beacon signals clear, fortify walls and clear the countryside, and thereby blunt their edge."
translations.idiomatic: Tighten discipline, keep the beacon lines clear, fortify the walls and clear the countryside—that is how to blunt their momentum."

sentences.zh: 時方銳意討之，既而諸將多覆軍者，久之無功，卒封元昊為夏國主，如育所議。

translations.literal: The court was then intent on campaigning against him. Before long many generals lost their armies. After a long time without success, Yuanhao was finally enfeoffed as Lord of the State of Xia, as Yu had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then bent on war. Generals soon lost whole armies, and after years of failure Yuanhao was enfeoffed as ruler of Xia—just as Yu had urged from the start.

sentences.zh: 育又上言：「天下久安，務因循而厭生事，政令紀綱，邊防機要，置不復修，一有邊警，則倉皇莫知所為，殆稍安靜，則又無敢輒言者。

translations.literal: Yu submitted again: "The realm has long been at peace; officials cling to routine and dislike raising issues. Edicts, discipline, frontier defenses, and vital measures are left unrepaired. Once a frontier alarm arises, they panic and do not know what to do; when things grow slightly calm again, none dare speak up.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted again: "After so long a peace, the realm clings to routine and dislikes raising new business. Government orders and discipline, frontier defenses, and essential measures have all been set aside and left unrepaired. At the first alarm on the border, everyone panics and has no idea what to do; once things grow even slightly quiet again, no one dares speak up.

sentences.zh: 若政令修，紀綱肅，財用富，恩信給，賞罰明，將帥練習，士卒精銳，則四夷望風，自無他志。

translations.literal: If edicts are well ordered, discipline is strict, resources are ample, favor and trust are extended, rewards and punishments are clear, generals are trained, and soldiers are keen, then the four barbarians will turn at the wind and of themselves have no other designs.
translations.idiomatic: If the laws are sound, discipline firm, the treasury full, grace and trust abundant, rewards and punishments clear, commanders well drilled, and troops sharp, the frontier peoples will submit at a glance and harbor no other ambitions.

sentences.zh: 若一不備，則乘間而起矣。」

translations.literal: If even one of these is lacking, they will seize the opportunity and rise."
translations.idiomatic: Let any one of these fail, and they will seize the moment to rise."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「漢通西域諸國，斷匈奴右臂。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Han opened relations with the states of the Western Regions, it severed the Xiongnu's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When the Han opened the Western Regions, they cut off the Xiongnu's right arm.

sentences.zh: 諸戎內附，雖有桀黠，不敢獨叛。

translations.literal: When the various Rong submitted inward, even if some were fierce and cunning, none dared rebel alone.
translations.idiomatic: With the tribes submitted to the court, even the fiercest among them dared not rebel on their own.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗嘗賜回鶻可汗並其相手書，納其貢奉，厚以金帛。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang once bestowed autograph letters on the Uyghur khan and his chancellor, accepted their tribute, and rewarded them generously with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang once sent personal letters to the Uyghur khan and his chancellor, accepted their tribute, and lavished gold and silk upon them.

sentences.zh: 真宗命潘羅支攻殺李繼遷，而德明乃降。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong ordered Pan Luozhi to attack and kill Li Jiqian, and then Deming submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong had Pan Luozhi strike down Li Jiqian, and only then did Deming surrender.

sentences.zh: 元昊第見朝廷比年與西域諸戎不通朝貢，乃得以利啗鄰境，固其巢穴，無肘腋之患。

translations.literal: Yuanhao has only seen that in recent years the court has not exchanged tribute with the various Rong of the Western Regions, and so he has been able to use profit to win over neighboring territories, secure his nest, and have no trouble at his flanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao has watched the court neglect the Western Regions for years, bribe neighboring tribes, fortify his base, and face no threat at his flanks.

sentences.zh: 跳梁猖獗，彼得以肆而不顧矣。

translations.literal: Leaping about in insolence, he has been able to run riot without regard for anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Rioting unchecked, he has been free to run wild without fear of reprisal.

sentences.zh: 請募士諭唃廝囉及他蕃部，離散其黨與，使並力以攻，而均其恩賜，此伐謀之要也。」

translations.literal: I ask that men be recruited to instruct Gusiluo and other frontier tribes, scatter his partisans, make them join forces to attack him, and distribute favors evenly—this is the essential of attacking his plans."
translations.idiomatic: Recruit envoys to win over Gusiluo and other tribes, break up his alliances, and have them attack him together while sharing our rewards evenly—that is the heart of defeating him by strategy."

sentences.zh: 因錄上真宗時通西域諸蕃事跡。

translations.literal: He thereupon compiled and submitted accounts of dealings with the various tribes of the Western Regions in Emperor Zhenzong's time.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled and submitted a record of how the court had dealt with the Western Regions under Emperor Zhenzong.

sentences.zh: 除同修起居注，遂知制誥，進翰林學士，累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Compiler of the Diary, then made Controller of Drafts, advanced to Hanlin Academician, and repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made associate compiler of the imperial diary, then controller of drafts, promoted to Hanlin academician, and eventually director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 契丹與元昊構兵，元昊求納款。

translations.literal: The Khitan and Yuanhao raised arms against each other, and Yuanhao sought to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and Yuanhao went to war, and Yuanhao asked to submit to the Song.

sentences.zh: 契丹使來請勿納元昊，朝廷未知所答。

translations.literal: A Khitan envoy came asking that Yuanhao not be accepted, and the court did not know how to reply.
translations.idiomatic: A Khitan envoy arrived asking the court not to accept Yuanhao, and the court was at a loss for a reply.

sentences.zh: 育因上疏曰：「契丹受恩，為日已久。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon submitted a memorial saying: "The Khitan have received our grace for many days already.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial: "The Khitan have enjoyed our favor for generations.

sentences.zh: 不可納一叛羌，失繼世兄弟之歡。

translations.literal: We must not accept one rebellious Qiang and lose the affection of brothers across generations.
translations.idiomatic: We must not welcome a rebellious Qiang chieftain and forfeit the goodwill of our hereditary allies.

sentences.zh: 今二蕃自鬥，鬥久不解，可觀形勢，乘機立功。

translations.literal: Now the two frontier peoples fight each other; if the fight is long unresolved, we may observe the situation and seize the moment to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: With the two frontier powers locked in combat, we should watch how the struggle unfolds and seize the moment to our advantage.

sentences.zh: 萬一過計，亟納元昊，臣恐契丹窺兵趙、魏，朝廷不得元昊毫髮之助，而太行東西，且有煙塵之警矣。

translations.literal: If by any misjudgment we hastily accept Yuanhao, I fear the Khitan will spy for troops in Zhao and Wei, the court will receive not the slightest help from Yuanhao, and east and west of the Taihang there will be alarms of war smoke.
translations.idiomatic: If we rashly accept Yuanhao, the Khitan may march on Zhao and Wei, Yuanhao will give us no help at all, and war smoke will rise on both sides of the Taihang range.

sentences.zh: 宜使人諭元昊曰：『契丹汝世姻，一旦自絕，力屈而歸我，我所疑也，若無他者，當順契丹如故，然後許汝歸款。』

translations.literal: It is fitting to send someone to tell Yuanhao: 'The Khitan are your hereditary affines. If you break with them at once and, your strength spent, come to us, that is what I suspect. If you have no other design, you should submit to the Khitan as before; only then will I permit your surrender.'
translations.idiomatic: Send an envoy to Yuanhao: 'The Khitan are your hereditary kin by marriage. If you break with them and come to us only because you are beaten, I will be suspicious. If you have no hidden aim, restore your ties with the Khitan as before—only then will I accept your submission.'

sentences.zh: 告契丹曰：『已詔元昊，如能投謝轅門，即聽內附；

translations.literal: Tell the Khitan: 'I have already issued an edict to Yuanhao that if he can come to the camp gate to submit, he will be allowed to attach inward;
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Khitan: 'I have already told Yuanhao that if he comes to our camp to surrender, he may submit;

sentences.zh: 若猶堅拒，當為討之。』

translations.literal: if he still stubbornly refuses, I will campaign against him.'
translations.idiomatic: if he still refuses, I will punish him.'

sentences.zh: 如此，則彼皆不能歸罪我矣。」

translations.literal: In this way neither side will be able to lay blame on us."
translations.idiomatic: In this way neither side can blame us."

sentences.zh: 於是召兩制，出契丹書，令兩制同上對，不易育議。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Two Institutes were summoned, the Khitan letter was produced, and the Two Institutes were ordered to present a joint response without altering Yu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned the drafters of the Two Institutes, produced the Khitan letter, and ordered them to frame a joint reply without changing Yu's plan.

sentences.zh: 尋知開封府。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 居數日，發大奸吏一人，流嶺外。

translations.literal: Within several days he exposed one great corrupt official and banished him beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he exposed a major corrupt official and exiled him beyond the Lingnan passes.

sentences.zh: 又得巨盜，積贓萬九千緡，獄具而輒再變，帝遣他吏按之，卒伏法。

translations.literal: He also caught a great bandit who had amassed illicit gains of nineteen thousand strings of cash. When the case was complete it was repeatedly changed; the emperor sent another official to investigate, and in the end [the bandit] was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: He also caught a major thief who had amassed nineteen thousand strings in stolen goods. After the case was closed the verdict kept being overturned, so the emperor sent another investigator—and the man was finally executed.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑多盜，育嚴賞功之法，嘗得盜而未賞者，一切賞之，以明不欺。

translations.literal: At the time famine brought many bandits. Yu tightened the law on rewarding merit. Those who had once caught bandits but had not been rewarded were all rewarded at once, to show that none would be cheated.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had bred many thieves. Yu enforced reward rules strictly and paid every officer who had caught a thief but never received a bounty, proving that no merit would go unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 慶曆五年，拜右諫議大夫、樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingli he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 5 he was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 居數月，改參知政事。

translations.literal: After several months he was transferred to Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 山東盜起，帝遣中使按視，還奏：「盜不足慮。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Shandong. The emperor sent a palace envoy to inspect and report back: "The bandits are not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Shandong. The emperor sent a palace envoy to investigate, who reported: "The bandits are no real threat.

sentences.zh: 兗州杜衍、鄆州富弼，山東人尊愛之，此可憂也。」

translations.literal: Du Yan of Yanzhou and Fu Bi of Yunzhou—the people of Shandong honor and love them. This is what is worrisome."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan in Yanzhou and Fu Bi in Yunzhou are deeply beloved in Shandong—that is what should worry us."

sentences.zh: 帝欲徙二人於淮南，育曰：「盜誠無足慮者，小人乘時以傾大臣，禍幾不可禦矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to transfer the two men to Huainan. Yu said, "The bandits truly are not worth worrying about. Petty men are seizing the moment to topple great ministers—a disaster nearly impossible to ward off."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to move both men to Huainan. Yu said, "The bandits are nothing—but petty men are using the moment to bring down great ministers. The harm would be nearly impossible to stop."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 章獻、章懿太后升祔真宗廟，議者請覃恩，且優賜軍士。

translations.literal: When Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi were enshrined alongside Emperor Zhenzong, debaters asked for a broad grant of grace and generous rewards for soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi were installed in Emperor Zhenzong's temple, some proposed a general amnesty and extra payments to the troops.

sentences.zh: 育曰：「無事而啟僥幸，誰為陛下建此議者，請治之。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "To stir up expectations of favor when there is no occasion—whoever advised Your Majesty on this, I ask that he be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "To encourage vain hopes when there is no cause—whoever proposed this to Your Majesty should be punished."

sentences.zh: 已而外人多怨執政者，帝以語輔臣，育曰：「此必建議者欲動搖上聽，臣以身許國，何憚此耶？」

translations.literal: Afterward many outsiders resented those in power. The emperor spoke of this to his chief ministers. Yu said, "This must be those who made the proposal trying to shake what reaches Your Majesty's ears. I have pledged my person to the state—why should I fear this?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon outsiders were blaming the chief ministers. When the emperor mentioned it, Yu said, "Those who made the proposal are surely trying to sway Your Majesty. I have given my life to the state—why should I fear their talk?"

sentences.zh: 向綬知永靜軍，為不法，疑通判江中立發其陰事，因構獄以危法中之，中立自經死。

translations.literal: Xiang Shou governed Yongjing Circuit and acted unlawfully. He suspected Vice Prefect Jiang Zhongli of exposing his secret affairs and therefore fabricated a case to endanger Zhongli by capital law. Zhongli hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shou, military commissioner of Yongjing, broke the law. Suspecting that Vice Prefect Jiang Zhongli had exposed his misdeeds, he framed a capital case against him, and Zhongli hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 綬宰相子，大臣有營助，欲傅輕法，育曰：「不殺綬，無以示天下。」

translations.literal: Shou was a prime minister's son; great ministers worked on his behalf and wished to apply a lighter statute. Yu said, "If Shou is not put to death, there is no way to show the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Shou was a prime minister's son, and powerful ministers lobbied for a lighter sentence. Yu said, "Unless Shou is executed, we cannot make an example to the realm."

sentences.zh: 卒減死一等，流南方。

translations.literal: In the end his death sentence was reduced one degree and he was banished to the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the death penalty was commuted one degree and he was exiled to the south.

sentences.zh: 御史唐詢請罷制科，帝刊其名付中書，育奏疏駁議，帝因諭輔臣曰：「彼上言者，乞從內批行下，今乃知欺罔也。」

translations.literal: Censor Tang Xun asked to abolish the decree-examination system. The emperor struck his name and sent it to the Secretariat. Yu submitted a memorial refuting the proposal. The emperor thereupon instructed the chief ministers: "That petitioner asked that it be carried out by inner draft. Now we know he was deceitful."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Xun petitioned to abolish the decree examinations. The emperor struck his name from the rolls and sent the matter to the Secretariat. Yu memorialized against it. The emperor told his chief ministers, "That man asked for an inner draft to carry this out—now we see he was deceiving us."

sentences.zh: 育曰：「非睿聽昭察，則挾邪蠹國，靡所不為。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Were it not for sagely hearing and clear scrutiny, those who harbor evil and harm the state would do anything.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Without Your Majesty's keen discernment, men who harbor evil and poison the state would stop at nothing.

sentences.zh: 願出姓名按劾，以明國法。」

translations.literal: I wish that the names be published and investigated according to law, to clarify the statutes of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Publish their names and investigate them under the law, so that the statutes of the realm are made clear."

sentences.zh: 育在政府，遇事敢言，與宰相賈昌朝數爭議上前，左右皆失色，育論辨不已，乃請曰：「臣所辨者，職也；

translations.literal: While Yu was in the government he spoke boldly on affairs. With the chief minister Jia Changchao he repeatedly argued before the throne until those at the emperor's side turned pale. Yu debated without cease and then requested: "What I debate is my office;
translations.idiomatic: In office Yu spoke boldly on every issue. He repeatedly argued with Chief Minister Jia Changchao before the throne until the attendants turned pale. Yu would not yield and finally said, "What I dispute is my duty;

sentences.zh: 顧力不勝，願罷臣職。」

translations.literal: yet seeing that my strength does not prevail, I wish to be dismissed from my post."
translations.idiomatic: but since I cannot prevail, I ask to be relieved of my post."

sentences.zh: 乃復以為樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon again made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reappointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年大旱，御史中丞高若訥曰：「大臣喧爭為不肅，故雨不時若。」

translations.literal: The next year there was great drought. Censor-in-Chief Gao Ruone said, "The great ministers' noisy quarrels are indecorous, and therefore the rain does not come in season."
translations.idiomatic: The next year a severe drought struck. Censor-in-chief Gao Ruone said, "The chief ministers' loud disputes have offended decorum, and so the rains do not come in season."

sentences.zh: 遂罷昌朝，而育歸給事中班。

translations.literal: Changchao was thereupon dismissed, and Yu returned to the roster of Supervising Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao was dismissed, and Yu was returned to the supervising secretaries' roster.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知許州，徙蔡州。

translations.literal: Before long he went out to govern Xuzhou and was transferred to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Xuzhou and then transferred to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 設伍保法，以檢制盜賊。

translations.literal: He established the Five-House Mutual-Security law to check and control bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted the mutual-security groups of five households to control banditry.

sentences.zh: 時京師有告妖人千數聚確山者，詔遣中使往召捕者十人。

translations.literal: At the time someone in the capital reported that a thousand sorcerers were gathered on Mount Que. An edict sent a palace envoy to summon ten men for arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Someone in the capital reported that a thousand sorcerers had gathered on Mount Que, and the court sent a palace envoy to summon ten men for arrest.

sentences.zh: 至，則以巡檢兵往索之，育曰：「使者欲得妖人還報邪？」

translations.literal: When they arrived, they were about to send patrol troops to search for them. Yu said, "Does the envoy wish to bring sorcerers back to report?"
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived they prepared to send patrol troops to seize the men. Yu asked, "Does the envoy simply need sorcerers to bring back in his report?"

translations.literal: He said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 曰：「育在此，雖不敏，聚千人境內，毋容不知。

translations.literal: Yu said, "While Yu is here, though I am not clever, if a thousand men gathered within the circuit, I could not fail to know.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "While I am here, however dull I may be, a thousand men could not gather in my jurisdiction without my knowing it.

sentences.zh: 此特鄉民用浮圖法相聚，以利錢財爾，一弓手召之，可致也。

translations.literal: This is merely villagers gathering by Buddhist methods to profit from money. One bowman could summon them and they would come.
translations.idiomatic: These are only villagers meeting in Buddhist fashion to raise money. One constable could summon them—they would come at once.

sentences.zh: 今以兵往，人相驚疑，請留毋往。」

translations.literal: If troops go now, people will alarm and suspect one another. I ask that they stay and not go."
translations.idiomatic: Send troops now and you will only spread panic. Please stay your hand."

sentences.zh: 中使以為然。

translations.literal: The palace envoy thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy agreed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召十人者至，械送闕下，皆無罪釋之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the ten summoned men arrived, were sent in shackles to the palace, and all were released without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ten men were brought in chains to the capital, found innocent, and released.

sentences.zh: 而告者伏辜。

translations.literal: The accuser then suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser was punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 尋以資政殿學士知河南府，徙陝州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, as Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance he governed Henan Prefecture and was transferred to Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and prefect of Henan, then transferred to Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 上書論詔獄曰：「先王凝旒黈纊，不欲聞見人之過失也。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on imperially ordered cases, saying: "The former kings drew the tassels of their caps before their eyes and did not wish to hear or see people's faults.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on imperially ordered prosecutions: "The ancient kings veiled their eyes with their cap tassels because they did not wish to hear or see the faults of others.

sentences.zh: 設有罪，即屬之有司。

translations.literal: If there was guilt, they entrusted it to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: When guilt existed, they left it to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 楊儀嘗為三司判官，近自御史臺移劾都亭驛，械縛過市，人人不測為何等大獄。

translations.literal: Yang Yi had once been a controller in the Three Departments. Recently the Censorate transferred his case for impeachment to the Metropolitan Post Station. Shackled and bound he was led through the market; everyone wondered what sort of great case this was.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, once a controller in the fiscal commissions, was recently impeached by the Censorate and tried at the Metropolitan Post Station. Led through the streets in chains, no one could guess what grave crime was involved.

sentences.zh: 及聞案具，乃止請求常事。

translations.literal: When it was heard that the case was complete, it turned out to be only the usual matter of requests [for favors].
translations.idiomatic: When the case closed, it proved to be nothing more than the usual charge of improper solicitation.

sentences.zh: 使道路眾口紛紛竊議，朝廷之士，人皆自危，豈養廉恥、示敦厚之道哉？」

translations.literal: This made the roads and the multitude whisper in discussion; court gentlemen each felt himself in peril. How is this the way to nurture integrity and shame and display a generous and honest path?"
translations.idiomatic: The streets buzzed with rumor, and every official at court felt endangered. How does this nurture integrity or display a generous and honest government?"

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎、知永興軍，召兼翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and military commissioner of Yongxing Circuit, and summoned additionally as Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites and military commissioner of Yongxing, and recalled as Hanlin attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭，且請便郡。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of illness and also asked for a convenient prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He declined on grounds of illness and asked for a less demanding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝語大臣曰：「吳育剛正可用，第嫉惡太過耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor told the ministers, "Wu Yu is upright and can be used, only he hates evil too excessively."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Wu Yu is upright and capable, though he hates evil with excessive zeal."

sentences.zh: 因命知汝州，遣內侍賜以禁中良藥。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered him to govern Ruzhou and sent a palace attendant to bestow fine medicines from within the Forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Yu prefect of Ruzhou and sent a palace attendant with fine medicines from the imperial pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 會疾不已，又請居散地，以集賢院學士判西京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: As his illness did not cease, he again asked to dwell in a nominal post and was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies acting for the Western Capital's Retained Commission of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness persisted he asked for a lighter post and was made academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with concurrent charge of the Western Capital's retained censorate.

sentences.zh: 外臺舊不領民事，時張堯佐知河陽，民訟久不決，多詣育訴。

translations.literal: The outer commission had formerly not handled civil cases. At the time Zhang Yaozuo governed Heyang; the people's lawsuits long went unresolved, and many came to Yu to plead.
translations.idiomatic: The outer censorate had not traditionally handled civil suits, but Zhang Yaozuo was prefect of Heyang and left cases unresolved for so long that many plaintiffs came to Yu instead.

sentences.zh: 育為辨曲直，判書狀尾，堯佐畏懼奉行。

translations.literal: Yu judged right and wrong for them, wrote judgments at the end of the documents, and Yaozuo, in fear, carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu decided their cases and signed the judgments at the foot of each petition; Yaozuo, intimidated, enforced them.

sentences.zh: 復為資政殿學士兼翰林侍讀學士、知陝州，進資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was again made Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and concurrent Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician, governing Shaanzhou, and was advanced to Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and Hanlin attendant reader, with appointment as prefect of Shaanzhou, and was promoted to grand academician of that hall.

sentences.zh: 召還，判尚書都省。

translations.literal: He was recalled and given concurrent charge of the Secretariat of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve concurrently as chief of the Secretariat of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 一日，侍讀禁中，帝因語及「臣下毀譽，多出愛憎，卿所當慎也。」

translations.literal: One day, while attending the emperor's reading within the Forbidden precincts, the emperor spoke of how "slander and praise of ministers mostly arise from love and hatred—you must be careful of this."
translations.idiomatic: One day, while reading with the emperor in the palace, the emperor remarked, "Praise and blame of ministers usually spring from personal liking and dislike—you must be careful of that."

sentences.zh: 育曰：「知而形之言，不若察而行之事。

translations.literal: Yu said: "To know and give it form in words is not as good as to observe carefully and carry it out in deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu said, "Knowing a thing and putting it into words is inferior to discerning it and embodying it in action.

sentences.zh: 聖主之行，如日月之明。

translations.literal: The conduct of a sage ruler is like the brightness of the sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: A sagely sovereign's conduct shines like the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 進一人，使人皆知其善，出一人，使人皆曉其惡，則陰邪不能構害，公正可以自立，百王之要道也。」

translations.literal: When he advances one person, he causes all to know that person's goodness; when he dismisses one, he causes all to understand that person's evil—then hidden wickedness cannot contrive harm, and impartial justice can establish itself; it is the essential path of a hundred kings."
translations.idiomatic: When promoting someone, let all know his merit; when removing someone, let all see his fault—then covert malice cannot plot harm and fairness stands firm: the cardinal principle of kings since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 帝數欲大用，為諫官劉元瑜誣奏育在河南嘗貸民出息錢。

translations.literal: The Emperor several times wished to employ him in great capacity, but remonstrance official Liu Yuanyu falsely memorialized that Yu had in Henan once lent the people money at interest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly meant to give him major responsibilities, but censor Liu Yuanyu falsely charged that Yu had in Henan lent money to commoners at interest.

sentences.zh: 久之，除宣徽南院使、鄜延路經略安撫使、判延州。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was appointed Southern Commissioner of the Xuanhui Bureau, Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner of the Zhenyan Circuit, and concurrent magistrate of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was made Commissioner of the Southern Xuanhui Bureau, frontier commissioner for Zhenyan, and prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 夏人既稱臣，而幷邊種落數侵耕為患。

translations.literal: The Xia people having already submitted as vassals, yet the tribal groups along the border of Bing repeatedly encroached on plowing as a nuisance.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Western Xia had submitted, border tribes kept raiding farms and causing trouble.

sentences.zh: 龐籍守幷州，欲築堡備之，育謂：「要契未明而亟城，則羌人必爭，爭而受患者必麟府也。」

translations.literal: Pang Ji was defending Bing Prefecture and wished to build forts to guard against them; Yu said: "Before the covenant terms are clear, yet hastily to wall cities—the Qiang will surely contend, and if they contend the one who suffers harm will surely be Lin Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji, holding Bingzhou, wanted to build forts; Yu said, "If we rush to fortify before agreements are settled, the Qiang will resist—and Lin and Fu prefectures will bear the cost."

sentences.zh: 移文河東，又遺籍手書及疏於朝，不報。

translations.literal: He sent official correspondence to Hedong, and also sent Pang Ji a personal letter and a memorial to court; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote officially to Hedong and sent Pang Ji a personal letter plus a memorial to the throne, all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 既而夏人果犯河外，陷驍將郭恩，而太原將佐皆得罪去。

translations.literal: Before long the Xia people indeed violated the region outside the Yellow River, destroyed the fierce general Guo En, and the officers and aides at Taiyuan were all punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Xia attacked west of the river, defeated the crack general Guo En, and Taiyuan's command staff were all dismissed in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 疾復作，辭不任邊事，求解宣徽使，復以為資政殿大學士、尚書左丞、知河中府，徙河南。

translations.literal: His illness recurred; he declined border duties, requested release from the Xuanhui commissioner post, and was again made Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, prefect of Hezhong—then transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Illness returned; he refused frontier service, resigned the Xuanhui post, and was reassigned as Zizheng academician, vice minister of Personnel, and prefect of Hezhong, later Henan.

sentences.zh: 病革，視事如平日，因閱囚辨非罪，竄舞文吏二人。

translations.literal: When critically ill, he handled affairs as on ordinary days; while reviewing prisoners he distinguished those not guilty and banished two clerks who twisted the law.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he still governed as usual, reviewed prisoners, freed the innocent, and banished two corrupt clerks.

sentences.zh: 已而卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died, age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，諡「正肅」。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Minister of Personnel; posthumous title "Upright and Stern."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel with the posthumous title "Zhengsu" (Upright and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 育性明果，所至作條教，簡疏易行而不可犯。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was bright and decisive; wherever he went he made regulations—simple, sparse, easy to carry out, yet not to be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was sharp and resolute; everywhere he posted concise rules that were easy to follow yet never breached.

sentences.zh: 遇事不妄發，發即人不能撓。

translations.literal: On matters he did not act rashly; when he did act, people could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: He never moved without cause; once he moved, no one could sway him.

sentences.zh: 辨論明白，使人聽之不疑。

translations.literal: His discourse was lucid, causing listeners not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He argued with such clarity that listeners were left without doubt.

sentences.zh: 初尹開封，范仲淹在政府，因事與仲淹忤。

translations.literal: At first when he governed Kaifeng, Fan Zhongyan was in the government; over an affair he clashed with Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Early as Kaifeng intendant he clashed with Fan Zhongyan in the cabinet over policy.

sentences.zh: 既而仲淹安撫河東，有奏請，多為任事者所沮，育取可行者固行之。

translations.literal: Later Zhongyan pacified Hedong; when he had memorial requests, many were blocked by men in charge of affairs—Yu took those feasible and firmly carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan later pacified Hedong, many of his proposals were blocked—Yu implemented those he found workable anyway.

sentences.zh: 其在二府，待問以列卿奉朝請，育不自安，請罷去，不聽。

translations.literal: In the Two Departments he treated Dai Wen as a ranked minister attending court audiences—Yu was ill at ease and requested to be relieved; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Departments he treated Dai Wen with full ministerial courtesies—uneasy, Yu asked to resign but was refused.

sentences.zh: 及出帥永興，時待問尚亡恙，肩輿迎侍，時人榮之。

translations.literal: When he went out as military commissioner of Yongxing, at that time Dai Wen was still in good health; he welcomed and attended him in a shoulder-borne sedan—men of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he took command at Yongxing, Dai Wen was still hale; Yu received him in a sedan chair—a point of pride among contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 晚年在西臺，與宋庠相唱酬，追裴、白遺事至數百篇。

translations.literal: In his later years on the Western Terrace he exchanged verses with Song Qi, recalling Pei and Bai's legacy to several hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: In later years on the Western Terrace he and Song Qi exchanged hundreds of poems in the vein of Pei Xingjian and Bai Juyi.

sentences.zh: 體素羸，少時力學，得心疾。

translations.literal: His constitution was always frail; in youth he studied strenuously and contracted a heart ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally slight of build, he drove himself in youth and developed heart trouble.

sentences.zh: 後得古方，和丹砂餌之，大醉，一夕而愈。

translations.literal: Later he obtained an ancient prescription, mixed cinnabar and took it as medicine, became greatly drunk, and in one night recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He later took a cinnabar remedy from an old formula, fell into a deep stupor, and awoke cured overnight.

sentences.zh: 後數發，每發數十日乃已。

translations.literal: Later it recurred several times; each recurrence lasted several tens of days before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The malady recurred repeatedly, each bout lasting weeks.

sentences.zh: 有集五十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings of fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 弟充，為宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chong became a grand councilor and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wu Chong, who became chief minister, has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宋綬，字公垂，趙州平棘人。

translations.literal: Song Shou, styled Gongchui, a man of Pingji in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shou (courtesy name Gongchui) was from Pingji in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 父皋，尚書度支員外郎、直集賢院。

translations.literal: His father Gao was Outer Vice Director of the Revenue Section in the Ministry of Works and Commissioner of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Song Gao served as vice director of revenue and Jixian academician.

sentences.zh: 綬幼聰警，額有奇骨，為外祖楊徽之所器愛。

translations.literal: Shou in youth was clever and alert, his forehead having remarkable bone structure, and was prized and loved by his maternal grandfather Yang Huizhi.
translations.idiomatic: As a child Shou was precocious, with striking features, and was cherished by his maternal grandfather Yang Huizhi.

sentences.zh: 徽之無子，家藏書悉與綬。

translations.literal: Huizhi had no son; all books in the family collection he gave to Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, Huizhi bequeathed his entire library to Shou.

sentences.zh: 綬母亦知書，每躬自訓教，以故博通經史百家，文章為一時所尚。

translations.literal: Shou's mother also knew books; each time she personally instructed him—thus he thoroughly penetrated the classics, histories, and a hundred schools; his writings were admired by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His literate mother tutored him herself; he mastered the classics and all learning, and his prose was the age's standard.

sentences.zh: 初，徽之卒，遺奏補太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Huizhi died, he left a memorial petitioning that [Shou] be appointed temple attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizhi died, he left a memorial petitioning that Shou be appointed temple attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 年十五，召試中書，真宗愛其文，遷大理評事，聽於秘閣讀書。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat; Emperor Zhenzong admired his writing, promoted him to Evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review, and permitted him to read in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat; Emperor Zhenzong admired his writing, made him evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review, and allowed him to read in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，復試學士院，為集賢校理，與父皋同職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was again examined at the Hanlin Academy, made collator of the Jixian Academy, and held the same post as his father Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was examined again at the Hanlin Academy, made Jixian collator, and held the same post as his father Gao.

sentences.zh: 後賜同進士出身，遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Later he was granted jinshi status by special favor and promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted jinshi status by special favor and promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 及祀汾陰，召赴行在，與錢易、陳越、劉筠集所過地志、風物、故實，每舍止即以奏。

translations.literal: When the Fengyin sacrifice was performed, he was summoned to the traveling court; with Qian Yi, Chen Yue, and Liu Yun he collected local gazetteers, scenery, and historical facts along the route, submitting a memorial at every stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fengyin sacrifice was performed, he was summoned to the traveling court; with Qian Yi, Chen Yue, and Liu Yun he collected local gazetteers, scenery, and historical facts along the route, submitting a memorial at every stop.

sentences.zh: 將祠亳州太清宮，以簽書亳州判官事，入為左正言、同判太常禮院。

translations.literal: When the Taqing Palace at Bozhou was to be sacrificed to, he served as acting Bozhou vice prefect, then entered court as Left Remonstrator and concurrent deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taqing Palace at Bozhou was to be sacrificed to, he served as acting Bozhou vice prefect, then entered court as left remonstrator and deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久之，判三司憑由司。

translations.literal: After some time he was made director of the Three Offices Certificates Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made director of the Three Offices Certificates Bureau.

sentences.zh: 建言：「比歲下赦令釋逋負，後期未報者六十八州。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In recent years amnesty edicts have released overdue obligations, yet sixty-eight prefectures have not reported by the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "In recent years amnesty edicts have released overdue obligations, yet sixty-eight prefectures have not reported by the deadline.

sentences.zh: 請於諸路選官考核，期半月以聞。」

translations.literal: I ask that officials be selected on each circuit to verify accounts, with a deadline of half a month to report."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that officials be selected on each circuit to verify accounts, with a deadline of half a month to report."

sentences.zh: 於是脫械繫三千二百人，蠲積負數百萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon three thousand two hundred people were freed from shackles, and accumulated obligations in the millions were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon three thousand two hundred people were freed from shackles, and accumulated obligations in the millions were remitted.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥、判吏部流內銓兼史館修撰、玉清昭應宮判官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Edicts, concurrent judge of the Personnel Ministry's inward flow selection, joint Historiography Compiler, and judge of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of edicts, head of personnel selection, historiographer, and commissioner of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部郎中、權直學士院，同修《真宗實錄》，進左司郎中，遂為翰林學士兼侍讀學士、勾當三班院。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, acting director of the Hanlin Academy, joint compiler of the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhenzong, advanced to Left Bureau Director, and then became Hanlin Academician with concurrent Lecturing Academician and superintendent of the Third Class Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ministry of Revenue to acting head of the Hanlin Academy, helped compile the Veritable Records of Zhenzong, and became Hanlin academician, lecturer to the heir, and head of the Third Class Bureau.

sentences.zh: 始詔讀唐史，固求解三班以顓進講。

translations.literal: He was first ordered to read the Tang History; he firmly requested release from the Third Class Bureau in order to devote himself to lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to lecture on Tang history, he insisted on resigning the Third Class post to focus on teaching.

sentences.zh: 同修國史，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He jointly compiled the National History and was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the national history and was promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 昭應宮災，罷二學士。

translations.literal: When the Zhaoying Palace burned, both academicians were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Zhaoying Palace, both Hanlin posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復翰林學士。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was restored as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was reappointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 史成，遷尚書工部侍郎兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When the history was completed, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works with concurrent Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was finished, he became vice minister of Works and lecturer to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時太后猶稱制，五日一御承明殿，垂簾決事，而仁宗未嘗獨對群臣也。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager still held regency; every five days she attended the Chenming Hall, drew the curtain and decided affairs—and Emperor Renzong had never yet faced the ministers alone.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager still ruled; every five days she held court behind a screen at Chenming Hall, and Renzong had never yet met his ministers alone.

sentences.zh: 綬奏言：「唐先天中，睿宗為太上皇，五日一受朝，處分軍國重務，除三品以下官，決徒刑。

translations.literal: Shou memorialized: "In the Xiantian era of Tang, Emperor Ruizong was Retired Emperor; every five days he received court audience, disposed of military and state weighty affairs, appointed officials below the third rank, and decided penal servitude cases.
translations.idiomatic: Shou submitted: "Under Tang Xiantian, Ruizong as retired emperor held audience every five days, handled state and military affairs, appointed officials below third rank, and adjudicated penal cases.

sentences.zh: 宜約先天制度，令群臣對前殿，非軍國大事，除拜皆前殿取旨。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow roughly the Xiantian system, causing the ministers to face audience in the front hall; for matters that are not military or state great affairs, all appointments and dismissals should receive imperial instruction in the front hall."
translations.idiomatic: He urged adopting the Xiantian precedent: ministers should attend the front hall, and all appointments short of major state matters should receive the emperor's approval there."

sentences.zh: 書上，忤太后意，改龍圖閣學士，出知應天府。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, it offended the Empress Dowager's intent; he was changed to Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and sent out as prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial angered the dowager; he was demoted to Dragon Diagram academician and sent to govern Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，帝思綬言，召還，將大用，而宰相張士遜沮止之，復加翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, the Emperor recalled Shou's words, summoned him back, and was about to employ him greatly—but Grand Councilor Zhang Shixun obstructed and stopped it; he was again added as Hanlin Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After the dowager's death the emperor recalled Shou's advice and summoned him back for high office, but chief minister Zhang Shixun blocked it; Shou was reappointed Hanlin lecturer instead.

sentences.zh: 詔定章獻明肅、章懿太后祔廟禮，綬援《春秋》考仲子之宮、唐坤儀廟故事，請別築宮曰奉慈廟以安神主，事多采用。

translations.literal: An edict fixed the rites for enshrining the spirit tablets of Empresses Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu and Zhangyi in the ancestral temple; Shou cited the Spring and Autumn Annals' "Examining the Palace of Zhongzi" and Tang precedents for the Kunyi Temple, requesting a separate hall called the Temple of Filial Devotion to install the spirit tablets—most of his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to set rites for the two dowager empresses' enshrinement, Shou cited Spring and Autumn and Tang Kunyi Temple precedents and proposed a separate Filial Devotion Temple for their tablets—largely adopted.

sentences.zh: 始置端明殿學士，以命綬，綬固辭。

translations.literal: When the Duanming Hall Academician post was first established, it was conferred on Shou; Shou firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the new Duanming Hall academician post was created, Shou was offered it but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又言：「帝王御天下，在總攬威柄。

translations.literal: He also said: "An emperor and king ruling all under Heaven lies in gathering and wielding authority.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "A ruler governs the realm by holding authority firmly in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 而一紀以來，令出簾帷。

translations.literal: Yet for a full twelve-year cycle commands have issued from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for twelve years orders had issued from behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 自陛下躬親萬務，內外延首，思見聖政，宜懲違革弊，以新百姓之耳目。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty personally attends to the myriad affairs, within and without all stretch their necks, thinking to see sagely governance—it is fitting to punish violations and reform abuses, to renew the eyes and ears of the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the reins, court and country alike await true governance; punish abuses and reform old ills to show the people a new order.

sentences.zh: 而賞罰號令，未能有過於前日，豈非三事大臣不能推心悉力，以輔陛下之治耶？

translations.literal: Yet rewards, punishments, and commands have not been able to surpass those of former days—is it not that the Three Affairs grand ministers cannot open their hearts and exhaust their strength to assist Your Majesty's governance?
translations.idiomatic: Yet rewards and orders have not improved on the regency era—can the chief ministers not give their full hearts to assist Your Majesty's rule?

sentences.zh: 頃太后朝多吝除拜，而邪幸或徑取升擢，議者謂恩出太后。

translations.literal: In the recent Empress Dowager court many appointments were stingily withheld, yet wicked favorites sometimes obtained promotion directly—discussants said favor issued from the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Under the dowager appointments had been scarce while favorites rose by back channels—critics said patronage came from her.

sentences.zh: 今恩賞雖行，又謂自大臣出，非大臣朋黨罔上，何以得此。

translations.literal: Now though favors and rewards are carried out, again it is said they issue from the grand ministers—if not that grand ministers' factional cliques deceive their superiors, how could they obtain this?
translations.idiomatic: Now favors flow again, yet critics say they come from the ministers—unless ministerial factions deceive the throne, how else could this happen?

sentences.zh: 朋黨之為朝廷患，古今同之。

translations.literal: Factional cliques as a harm to the court—ancient and modern are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Factionalism has plagued courts in every age.

sentences.zh: 或窺測帝旨，密令陳奏；

translations.literal: Some probe the Emperor's intent and secretly order memorials submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Some probe the emperor's mind and secretly direct memorials;

sentences.zh: 或附會己意，以進退人。

translations.literal: some attach to their own intent in advancing and dismissing people.
translations.idiomatic: others twist appointments to suit their own designs.

sentences.zh: 大官市恩以招權，小人趨利以售進，此風寖長，有蠹邦政。

translations.literal: Great officials trade favors to attract power; petty men rush for profit to sell advancement—this wind gradually grows long and has the power to harm state governance.
translations.idiomatic: Great officials trade favors for power; petty men buy advancement for profit—this trend grows and poisons government.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗曰：『國家無外憂必有內患。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once said: "When the state has no external worry, there must be internal trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once said, "When a state faces no external threat, internal trouble is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 外憂不過邊事，皆可預防；

translations.literal: External worry is no more than border affairs—all can be guarded against in advance;
translations.idiomatic: External threats are only border troubles, all preventable;

sentences.zh: 奸邪共濟為內患，深可懼也。』

translations.literal: wicked and evil men aiding each other as internal trouble—deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: but wicked men acting in concert within—deeply to be feared.

sentences.zh: 真宗亦曰：『唐朋黨尤盛，王室遂卑。』

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong also said: "Tang factional cliques were especially flourishing, and the royal house thus became low."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong also said, "Tang factionalism ran rampant, and the throne was brought low."

sentences.zh: 願陛下思祖宗之訓，念王業艱難，整齊綱紀，正在今日。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to reflect on the ancestral instructions, recall the hardship of the royal enterprise, and put in order laws and discipline—the time is precisely today."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty heed the founders' teaching, remember how hard the throne was won, and restore discipline—there is no time but now."

sentences.zh: 張士遜罷，乃拜綬參知政事。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shixun was dismissed, Shou was then appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Shixun was removed, Shou was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，有詔罷修寺觀，而章惠太后以舊宅為道觀，諫官、御史言之。

translations.literal: At first there was an edict to cease building temples and monasteries, yet Empress Dowager Zhanghui converted her old residence into a Daoist abbey—remonstrance officials and censors spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had halted temple construction, but Empress Dowager Zhanghui turned her old residence into a Daoist abbey—censors protested.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此太后奩中物也，諫官、御史欲邀名邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is from the Empress Dowager's trousseau—do remonstrance officials and censors wish to seek reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This was the dowager's own property—are the censors just seeking fame?"

sentences.zh: 綬進曰：「彼豈知太后所為哉。

translations.literal: Shou advanced and said: "How would they know what the Empress Dowager did?
translations.idiomatic: Shou replied, "How would they know what the dowager intended?

sentences.zh: 第見興土木違近詔，即論奏之。

translations.literal: They merely saw construction of earth and timber violating the recent edict and at once memorialized on it.
translations.idiomatic: They saw construction violating the recent edict and reported it—that is all.

sentences.zh: 且事有疑似，彼猶指為過，或陛下有大闕失，近臣雖不言，然傳聞四方，為聖政之累，何可忽也。

translations.literal: Moreover when affairs have seeming resemblance, they still point to them as faults—or if Your Majesty has great omissions and failures, though close ministers do not speak, yet it is transmitted and heard in the four directions, becoming a burden on sagely governance—how can it be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: When matters look questionable they still criticize them; if Your Majesty errs gravely and close advisers stay silent, rumor spreads everywhere and mars your rule—how can that be ignored?

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂唐太宗為諫官所詆，不以為愧。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu once said that when Emperor Taizong was slandered by remonstrance officials, he did not regard it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu noted that Taizong took no shame when censors criticized him.

sentences.zh: 何若動無過舉，使無得而言哉？」

translations.literal: How much better to act without fault, causing them to have nothing to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Better still to act without fault so they have nothing to say."

sentences.zh: 郭皇后廢，帝命綬作詔曰：「當求德閥，以稱坤儀。」

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, the Emperor ordered Shou to draft an edict saying: "One should seek moral virtue and eminent lineage to match the empress's station."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed, the emperor had Shou draft an edict: "Seek virtue and noble lineage worthy of the empress's station."

sentences.zh: 既而左右引富人陳氏女入宮，綬曰：「陛下乃欲以賤者正位中宮，不亦與前日詔語戾乎？」

translations.literal: Before long attendants led in the daughter of the wealthy Chen family to the palace; Shou said: "Your Majesty now wishes to install a low-born person in the central palace—is this not also at odds with the edict language of the other day?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon attendants brought a merchant's daughter, Chen, into the palace; Shou said, "Your Majesty would seat a woman of low birth in the inner palace—does that not contradict your own edict?"

sentences.zh: 後數日，王曾入對，又論奏之。

translations.literal: Several days later Wang Zeng entered audience and again memorialized on it.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Wang Zeng remonstrated on the same matter.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「宋綬亦如此言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Song Shou also spoke thus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Song Shou said the same."

sentences.zh: 時大臣繼有論者，卒罷之。

translations.literal: At that time grand ministers in succession had discourses; in the end it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Other ministers joined in, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝春秋富，天下久無事，綬慮宴樂有漸，乃言：「人心逸於久安，而患害生於所忽。

translations.literal: The Emperor's years were abundant, and all under Heaven had long been without affairs; Shou feared feasting and pleasure would gradually increase, and thus said: "Human hearts grow lax in long peace, yet harm arises from what is neglected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in his prime and the realm had known peace for years; Shou feared growing indulgence and said, "Men grow lax in long peace, yet disaster springs from what is overlooked.

sentences.zh: 故立防於無事，銷變於未萌。

translations.literal: Therefore establish defenses when there are no affairs, and dissolve change before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore set guards in quiet times and quell trouble before it sprouts.

sentences.zh: 事至而應，不亦殆歟？

translations.literal: To wait until affairs arrive and then respond—is that not perilous?
translations.idiomatic: To react only when crisis strikes—is that not perilous?

sentences.zh: 臣願飭勵群司，不以承平自怠。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to admonish and encourage all offices not to grow slack because of enduring peace."
translations.idiomatic: I urge every office not to slacken in this era of peace."

sentences.zh: 又上：「馭下之道有三：臨事尚乎守，當機貴乎斷，兆謀先乎密。

translations.literal: He also submitted: "The way of governing subordinates has three points: in facing affairs esteem steadfastness; at the critical moment value decisiveness; at the first omen of planning put secrecy first.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted: "Governing men requires three things: steadfastness in routine affairs, decisiveness at the critical moment, and secrecy at the first sign of planning.

sentences.zh: 能守則奸不能移，能斷則邪不能惑，能密則事不能撓。

translations.literal: If able to be steadfast, then treachery cannot shift you; if able to be decisive, then evil cannot bewilder you; if able to be secret, then affairs cannot bend you.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfastness keeps treachery from swaying you; decisiveness keeps wickedness from confusing you; secrecy keeps affairs from being thwarted.

sentences.zh: 願陛下念之！

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to keep these in mind!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty keep these in mind!

sentences.zh: 至若深居燕間，聲味以調六氣，節宣以順四時，保養聖躬，宗社之休也。」

translations.literal: As for dwelling deeply in ease and leisure, using sound and flavor to harmonize the six qi, regulating discharge to accord with the four seasons, and nurturing the sacred person—it is the felicity of altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: As for resting in quiet, using music and diet to balance the body's energies and the seasons to preserve Your Majesty's health—that is the blessing of throne and state."

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時宰相呂夷簡、王曾論議數不同。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Councilors Lü Yijian and Wang Zeng in discussion and debate were often at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Lü Yijian and Wang Zeng often disagreed in council.

sentences.zh: 綬多是夷簡，而參知政事蔡齊間有所異，政事繇此依違不決，於是四人者皆罷。

translations.literal: Shou mostly sided with Yijian, while Vice Grand Councilor Cai Qi sometimes differed—state affairs from this wavered undecided, and thus all four men were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shou usually sided with Lü, while vice councilor Cai Qi sometimes dissented; policy stalled, and all four were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 綬以尚書左丞、資政殿學士留侍講筵，權判尚書都省。

translations.literal: Shou remained to attend the lecture hall as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Zizheng Hall Academician, with acting jurisdiction over the Ministry Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shou stayed on as left vice director and Zizheng academician to lecture the throne, with acting charge of the Ministry headquarters.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，加資政殿大學士，以禮部尚書知河南府。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was added Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall and made Minister of Rites with jurisdiction over Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made grand Zizheng academician and minister of Rites governing Henan.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，劉平、石元孫敗沒，帝以手詔賜大臣居外者，詢攻守之策。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao rebelled; Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated and lost; the Emperor with handwritten edict bestowed on grand ministers residing outside asked offensive and defensive strategies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled and Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated, the emperor sent handwritten edicts to ministers in the provinces asking for offensive and defensive plans.

sentences.zh: 綬畫十事以獻。

translations.literal: Shou drafted ten items and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Shou submitted a ten-point plan.

sentences.zh: 復召知樞密院事，遷兵部尚書、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was again summoned to direct the Bureau of Military Affairs, transferred to Minister of War, and made Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to minister of War, and made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時綬母尚在，綬既得疾，不視事，猶起居自力，區處後事。

translations.literal: At that time Shou's mother was still alive; Shou having fallen ill and not handling affairs, still rose and lay down by his own strength and arranged later matters.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was still alive; though ill and unable to attend court, he still rose each day and put his affairs in order.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈司徒兼侍中，諡「宣獻」。

translations.literal: Shortly he died; posthumously gifted Grand Mentor with concurrent Palace Attendant; posthumous title "Proclaiming and Offering."
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor and palace attendant, with the posthumous title "Xuanxian" (Proclaiming and Offering).

sentences.zh: 綬性孝謹清介，言動有常。

translations.literal: Shou's nature was filial, cautious, pure, and upright; speech and conduct had constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was filial, prudent, upright, and consistent in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 為兒童時，手不執錢。

translations.literal: When a child, his hands did not hold money.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he would not touch money.

sentences.zh: 家藏書萬餘卷，親自校讎，博通經史百家，其筆劄尤精妙。

translations.literal: The family collection held more than ten thousand juan of books; he personally collated them, thoroughly penetrating classics, histories, and a hundred schools; his brush writings were especially refined and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: His family library held over ten thousand volumes, which he collated himself; he mastered the classics and all learning, and his calligraphy was exceptionally fine.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大議論，多綬所裁定。

translations.literal: Great court debates were mostly adjudicated by Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Major court debates were largely settled by Shou.

sentences.zh: 楊億稱其文沈壯淳麗，曰：「吾殆不及也。」

translations.literal: Yang Yi praised his writings as deep, strong, pure, and beautiful, saying: "I am probably not his equal."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi praised his prose as deep, powerful, and elegant, saying, "I can scarcely match him."

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝多取所書字藏禁中。

translations.literal: When he died, the Emperor took many of the characters he had written and stored them within the Forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor collected many of his calligraphic works for the imperial collection.

sentences.zh: 初，郊祀，綬攝太僕卿。

translations.literal: At first, during suburban sacrifice, Shou acted as Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, at a suburban sacrifice, Shou served as acting Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 帝問儀物典故，占對辨洽，因上所撰《鹵簿圖》十卷。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked about ritual objects and classical precedents; he responded with fluent discrimination and thereupon submitted his compiled Ten Fascicles of Illustrations of the Imperial Escort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about ritual regalia and precedent; Shou answered fluently and presented his ten-fascicle Illustrated Imperial Escort.

sentences.zh: 子敏求。

translations.literal: His son was Minqiu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Song Minqiu.

sentences.zh: 子 敏求

translations.literal: Son: Minqiu
translations.idiomatic: Song Minqiu

sentences.zh: 敏求，字次道，賜進士及第，為館閣校勘。

translations.literal: Minqiu, style name Cidao, was granted jinshi with highest honors, and served as collator in the Hall of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Song Minqiu, courtesy name Cidao, received the jinshi degree with highest honors and was appointed collator in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 預蘇舜欽進奏院會，出簽書集慶軍判官。

translations.literal: He took part in Su Shunqin's Memorial Court gathering, then went out as acting secretary and military judge of Jiqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Su Shunqin's ill-fated Memorial Court gathering and was sent out as acting secretary and military affairs judge of the Jiqing Army.

sentences.zh: 王堯臣修《唐書》，以敏求習唐事，奏為編修官。

translations.literal: When Wang Yaochen was compiling the Tang History, because Minqiu was versed in Tang affairs, he was memorialized to serve as a compilation officer.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Yaochen was editing the Tang History, Minqiu was recommended as a compilation officer because of his expertise in Tang affairs.

sentences.zh: 持祖母喪，詔令居家修書。

translations.literal: Observing mourning for his grandmother, he was ordered to compile books at home.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his grandmother, he was ordered to continue compiling books at home.

sentences.zh: 卒喪，同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, he served as deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 石中立薨，子繼死，無他子。

translations.literal: Shi Zhongli died; his son Ji died, and there were no other sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhongli died; his son Ji died, leaving no other heirs.

sentences.zh: 其孫祖仁疑所服，下禮官議。

translations.literal: His grandson Zuren questioned what mourning garments to wear, and the matter was referred to the ritual officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zuren questioned what mourning to observe, and the matter was referred to the ritual officials.

sentences.zh: 敏求謂宜為服三年，當解官，斬衰。

translations.literal: Minqiu said they should observe three-year mourning, resign office, and wear zhan mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Minqiu argued they should observe three-year mourning, resign office, and wear zhan mourning.

sentences.zh: 同僚援據不一，判寺宋祁是其議，遂定為令。

translations.literal: Colleagues cited differing precedents; Director Song Qi agreed with his proposal, and it was fixed as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues cited differing precedents, but court director Song Qi agreed with Minqiu, and the rule was established.

sentences.zh: 加集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was additionally made collator of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Jixian collator.

sentences.zh: 從宋庠辟，通判西京。

translations.literal: Recruited by Song Xiang, he became vice prefect of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited by Song Xiang, he became vice prefect of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 為群牧度支判官。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the Pasturage Office revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the Pasturage Office revenue section.

sentences.zh: 墜馬傷足，出知亳州。

translations.literal: He fell from a horse and injured his foot, and was sent out as prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After falling from a horse and injuring his foot, he was sent out as prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 治平中，召為《仁宗實錄》檢討官，同修起居注、知制誥、判太常寺。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era he was summoned as collator of the Veritable Records of Emperor Renzong, joint compiler of the Diurnal Record, drafter of edicts, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping he was summoned as collator of the Veritable Records of Emperor Renzong, joint compiler of the Diurnal Record, drafter of edicts, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 英宗在殯，有言宗室服疏者可嫁娶，敏求以為大行未發引，不可。

translations.literal: While Yingzong lay in state, some said that imperial clansmen in loose mourning might marry; Minqiu held that the great funeral procession had not yet departed and that this was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Yingzong lay in state, some argued that imperial clansmen in lighter mourning might marry; Minqiu held that the great funeral procession had not yet departed and that this was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 逾年，又有言者。

translations.literal: After a year, there were speakers again.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the question was raised again.

sentences.zh: 敏求言宗室義服，服降而練，可嫁娶矣。

translations.literal: Minqiu said that for imperial clansmen in ceremonial mourning, once the mourning grade was lowered to the lian stage, marriage was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Minqiu argued that for imperial clansmen in ceremonial mourning, once the mourning grade was reduced to the lian stage, marriage was permissible.

sentences.zh: 坐前後議異，貶秩知絳州。

translations.literal: For differing opinions before and after, he was demoted in rank and made prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because his views before and after had differed, he was demoted and sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王珪、范鎮乞留之，使成《實錄》。

translations.literal: Wang Gui and Fan Zhen begged to retain him so that he might complete the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and Fan Zhen petitioned to keep him so he could finish the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「典禮，國之所重，而誤謬如是，安得無責。」

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "Rites are what the state esteems; with errors such as these, how can there be no accountability?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "Rites are among the state's greatest concerns; with errors such as these, how can there be no accountability?"

sentences.zh: 然敏求議初不誤，曾公亮惡禮院劉瑾附敏求為說，故因是去之。

translations.literal: Yet Minqiu's initial opinion had not been wrong; Zeng Gongliang hated Liu Jin of the ritual court, who sided with Minqiu's argument, and therefore removed him on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Minqiu's initial opinion had not been wrong; Zeng Gongliang resented Liu Jin of the ritual court, who had sided with Minqiu, and used this as the pretext for his removal.

sentences.zh: 是歲，即詔還。

translations.literal: That same year, an edict immediately recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was recalled by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 徐國公主以夫兄為侄奏官，敏求疏其亂天倫，執正之。

translations.literal: Princess Xu Guo memorialized to grant office to her husband's elder brother as if he were a nephew; Minqiu memorialized that this disordered human relations and upheld the proper standard.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xu Guo petitioned to grant office to her husband's elder brother as though he were a nephew; Minqiu memorialized against this violation of proper kinship and upheld the correct standard.

sentences.zh: 王安石惡呂公著，誣其言韓琦欲因人心，如趙鞅興晉陽之甲，以逐君側之惡，出之潁州。
