translations.literal: Wang Anshi hated Lü Gongzhu and slandered him, alleging that Han Qi wished to exploit popular sentiment, like Zhao Yang raising the arms of Jinyang to expel evil at the ruler's side, and sent him out to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi hated Lü Gongzhu and slandered him, alleging that Han Qi wished to exploit popular sentiment—as Zhao Yang had raised the arms of Jinyang to expel evil at the ruler's side—and had him transferred to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 敏求當草制，安石諭旨使明著罪狀，敏求但言敷陳失實，安石怒白於帝，命陳升之改其語，敏求請解職，未聽。

translations.literal: Minqiu was to draft the edict; Anshi instructed that the crimes be stated clearly; Minqiu wrote only that the statements were untrue; Anshi angrily reported this to the emperor and ordered Chen Shengzhi to revise the wording; Minqiu requested dismissal, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Minqiu was assigned to draft the edict, Anshi instructed him to state the charges explicitly; Minqiu wrote only that the allegations were false. Anshi angrily reported this to the emperor and had Chen Shengzhi revise the text. Minqiu asked to resign, but his request was denied.

sentences.zh: 會李定自秀州判官除御史，敏求封還詞頭，遂以本官右諫議大夫奉朝請。

translations.literal: When Li Ding was promoted from Xiuzhou judge to censor, Minqiu sealed and returned the draft appointment; he was then retained at his original rank as Right Remonstrator with attendance at court only.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ding was promoted from Xiuzhou judge to censor, Minqiu sealed and returned the appointment draft; he was then kept at his original rank as Right Remonstrator with attendance at court only.

sentences.zh: 策試賢良方正，孔文仲對語切直，擢置優等，安石愈怒，罷文仲。

translations.literal: In the examination for worthy and upright candidates, Kong Wenzho's answers were incisive and direct; he was placed in the superior grade; Anshi grew still angrier and dismissed Wenzho.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination for worthy and upright candidates, Kong Wenzho's answers were blunt and forthright; he was placed in the top grade. Anshi was further enraged and had Wenzho dismissed.

sentences.zh: 人為敏求懼，帝獨全護之，除史館修撰、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: People feared for Minqiu, but the emperor alone fully protected him and appointed him historiographer of the History Office and academician of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Others feared for Minqiu, but the emperor alone protected him and appointed him historiographer of the History Office and academician of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 鄧潤甫為帝言：「比群臣多尚告訐，非國家之美，宜登用敦厚之士，以變薄俗。」

translations.literal: Deng Runpu said to the emperor: "Recently many ministers esteem informing against others; this is not the state's glory. One should elevate sincere and generous men to change shallow customs."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Runpu told the emperor, "Lately many ministers have favored informing against one another, which is no credit to the state. Sincere and generous men should be promoted to change these shallow ways."

sentences.zh: 乃加敏求龍圖閣直學士，命修《兩朝正史》，掌均國公箋奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minqiu was made a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, ordered to compile the Standard History of Two Reigns, and put in charge of memorials for Duke Junguo.
translations.idiomatic: Minqiu was then made a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, charged with compiling the Standard History of Two Reigns and with handling memorials for Duke Junguo.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yuanfeng, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 特贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously gifted the title of Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敏求家藏書三萬卷，皆略誦習，熟於朝廷典故，士大夫疑議，必就正焉。

translations.literal: Minqiu's family collection held thirty thousand juan of books, all of which he had recited in outline; he was expert in court precedents, and whenever officials had doubts they would consult him.
translations.idiomatic: His family library held thirty thousand volumes, all of which he had read in outline; he was expert in court precedent, and officials with doubts invariably sought him out.

sentences.zh: 補唐武宗以下《六世實錄》百四十八卷，它所著書甚多，學者多諮之。

translations.literal: He supplemented the Veritable Records of Six Reigns from Emperor Wuzong of Tang in one hundred forty-eight fascicles; his other writings were numerous, and scholars often consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: He supplemented the Veritable Records of Six Reigns from Emperor Wuzong of Tang in one hundred forty-eight fascicles; he wrote many other works, and scholars often sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗建言：「河北、陝西、河東舉子，性樸茂，而辭藻不工，故登第者少。

translations.literal: He once memorialized: "Examinees from Hebei, Shaanxi, and Hedong are by nature plain and solid, but their rhetoric is not polished, and therefore few pass the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized, "Candidates from Hebei, Shaanxi, and Hedong are plain and solid by nature, but their literary polish is weak, and few therefore pass the examinations.

sentences.zh: 請令轉運使擇薦有行藝材武者，特官之，使人材參用，而士有可進之路。

translations.literal: He requested that transport commissioners select and recommend those with conduct, talent, and martial skill for special appointment, so that talent might be employed in combination and scholars have a path of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that transport commissioners recommend men of character, learning, and martial skill for special appointment, so that diverse talent might be used and scholars have a path to advancement.

sentences.zh: 又州郡有學舍而無學官，故士輕去鄉里以求師，請置學官。」

translations.literal: Moreover, prefectures and districts had school buildings but no instructors, so scholars readily left their home districts to seek teachers; he requested that school officers be appointed."
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that many prefectures had school buildings but no instructors, so scholars readily left home to seek teachers, and he asked that school officers be appointed."

sentences.zh: 後頗施行之。

translations.literal: These measures were later largely put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: These proposals were later largely implemented.

sentences.zh: 族弟昌言。

translations.literal: His younger clansman was Changyan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger clansman was Song Changyan.

sentences.zh: 族子 昌言

translations.literal: Clansman: Changyan
translations.idiomatic: Song Changyan

sentences.zh: 昌言，字仲謨，以蔭為澤州司理參軍。

translations.literal: Changyan, style name Zhongmo, by yin privilege became judicial aide of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan, courtesy name Zhongmo, entered office by yin privilege as judicial aide of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州有殺人獄，昌言疑其冤，堅請跡捕，果得真犯者。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a murder case; Changyan suspected a wrongful conviction and firmly requested that the trail be pursued; the true culprit was indeed obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture had a murder case, Changyan suspected a wrongful conviction and insisted on pursuing the trail until the real culprit was found.

sentences.zh: 稍遷河陰發運判官。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to transport intendant judge of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to transport intendant judge at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 自濟源之官，見道上棄屍若剮剝狀者甚眾，竊歎郡縣之不治。

translations.literal: Traveling from Jiyuan to his post, he saw many abandoned corpses on the road that looked as if they had been flayed and butchered, and privately sighed at the failure of prefectures and counties to govern.
translations.idiomatic: On his way from Jiyuan to his new post, he saw many abandoned corpses along the road that looked as if they had been flayed and butchered, and he lamented the failure of local government.

sentences.zh: 既至河陰，得凶盜六輩，殺人而鬻之，如是十餘年，掩其家，猶得執縛未殺者七人。

translations.literal: Once he reached Heyin, he obtained six vicious bandits who had killed people and sold the flesh, doing so for more than ten years; raiding their homes, he still seized seven persons not yet killed who were bound.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin he captured six vicious bandits who had killed people and sold the flesh for more than ten years; raiding their homes, he found seven victims still bound and not yet killed.

sentences.zh: 縣吏與市井少年共為胠橐，昌言窮治其淵藪，皆法外行之，而流其家人。

translations.literal: County clerks and market youths jointly plundered; Changyan thoroughly prosecuted their dens; all were executed outside the law, and their families were exiled.
translations.idiomatic: County clerks and market youths had joined in the plunder; Changyan thoroughly rooted out their dens, executed them all extra-legally, and exiled their families.

sentences.zh: 擢都水監丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervisor of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervisor of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，河決棗彊而北。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, the Yellow River broke through at Zaojiang and flowed north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era, the Yellow River broke through at Zaojiang and turned north.

sentences.zh: 昌言建議，欲於二股河口西岸新灘，立土約障水，使之東流。

translations.literal: Changyan proposed that at the new bar on the west bank of the mouth of the two channels, an earthen dike be built to block the water and make it flow east.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan proposed building an earthen dike on the new bar at the west bank of the two-channel mouth to block the river and force it eastward.

sentences.zh: 候稍深，即斷北流，縱出葫盧下流，以除恩、冀、深、瀛水患。

translations.literal: When the water grew somewhat deeper, the north flow would be cut off and released through the lower Hulu channel to eliminate flooding in En, Ji, Shen, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Once the channel had deepened, the north flow would be cut off and diverted through the lower Hulu channel to relieve flooding in En, Ji, Shen, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 提舉河渠王亞以為不可成，不如修生堤。

translations.literal: Wang Ya, commissioner of river works, held that it could not succeed and that it would be better to build living dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, commissioner of river works, argued that the plan could not succeed and that building living dikes would be better.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣翰林學士司馬光往視，如昌言策。

translations.literal: The court sent Hanlin academician Sima Guang to inspect; he agreed with Changyan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Hanlin academician Sima Guang to inspect the site; he endorsed Changyan's plan.

sentences.zh: 不兩月，決口塞。

translations.literal: Within less than two months, the breach was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 光奏昌言獨有功，若與同列均受賞，恐不足以勸。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized that Changyan alone had merit; if he received the same reward as his colleagues, it would probably not suffice as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Guang memorialized that Changyan alone deserved credit; if he received the same reward as his colleagues, it would scarcely encourage merit.

sentences.zh: 詔理提點刑獄資序，遷開封府推官、同判都水監。

translations.literal: An edict rectified his seniority in the circuit judicial commission; he was promoted to investigator of Kaifeng Prefecture and co-administrator of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: His seniority in the circuit judicial commission was regularized by edict, and he was promoted to investigator of Kaifeng Prefecture and co-administrator of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 汴水漲，昌言請塞訾家口。

translations.literal: When the Bian River rose, Changyan requested that Zijia Kou be sealed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian River rose, Changyan requested that Zijia Kou be sealed.

sentences.zh: 已而汴流絕，監丞侯叔獻唱為昌言罪，昌言懼，求知陝州。

translations.literal: Before long the Bian flow was cut off; supervisor Hou Shuxian led the charge blaming Changyan; Changyan feared and requested appointment as prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Bian River dried up; supervisor Hou Shuxian led the charge to blame Changyan. Fearing reprisal, Changyan asked to be made prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷濮、冀二州。

translations.literal: He served in succession in the two prefectures of Pu and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Pu and Ji.

sentences.zh: 河決曹村，召判都水監，往護河堤。

translations.literal: When the river broke at Caocun, he was summoned to judge the Directorate of Waterways and went to protect the river dikes.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke at Caocun, he was recalled to administer the Directorate of Waterways and sent to protect the dikes.

sentences.zh: 靈平埽成，轉少府監。

translations.literal: When the Lingping embankment was completed, he was transferred to the Minor Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lingping embankment was completed, he was transferred to the Minor Treasury.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈絹二百匹。

translations.literal: He died; two hundred bolts of silk were gifted.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 李若谷

translations.literal: Li Ruogu
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruogu

sentences.zh: 李若谷，字子淵，徐州豐人。

translations.literal: Li Ruogu, style name Ziyuan, was a native of Feng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruogu, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a native of Feng in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤遊學，依姻家趙況於洛下，遂葬父母緱氏。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he traveled to study and relied on his in-law Zhao Kuang at Luoyang; he thereupon buried his parents at Goushi.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he traveled to study and lived with his in-law Zhao Kuang in Luoyang, where he buried his parents at Goushi.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，補長社縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed aide of Changshe County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed aide of Changshe County.

sentences.zh: 州葺兵營，課民輸木，檄尉受之，而吏以不中程，多退斥，欲苛苦輸者，因以取賕；

translations.literal: The prefecture was repairing military barracks and levied timber from the people; an order was sent to the aide to receive it, but clerks, claiming it did not meet specifications, rejected much of it, wishing to harass those delivering so as to extort bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture repaired military barracks and levied timber from the people, the aide was ordered to receive deliveries; clerks rejected much of it as substandard, harassing contributors so they could extort bribes.

sentences.zh: 若谷度財，別其長短、大小為程，置庭中，使民自輸。

translations.literal: Ruogu assessed value, distinguished long and short and large and small as standards, placed them in the courtyard, and let the people deliver themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu assessed fair value, set standards by length and size, placed sample timbers in the courtyard, and let the people deliver their own loads.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺丞、知宜興縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to aide of the Court of Judicial Review and made magistrate of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made aide of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 官市湖洑茶，歲約戶稅為多少，率取足貧下，若谷始置籍備勾檢。

translations.literal: The government purchased Hufu tea; each year an amount was set according to household tax; they routinely took the full quota from the poor; Ruogu first established registers for audit and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The government purchased Hufu tea yearly according to household tax assessments and routinely took the full quota from the poorest households; Ruogu first established registers for audit and inspection.

sentences.zh: 茶惡者舊沒官，若谷使歸之民，許轉貿以償其數。

translations.literal: Inferior tea had formerly been confiscated by the government; Ruogu had it returned to the people and permitted trade in exchange to make up the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Inferior tea had formerly been confiscated by the state; Ruogu returned it to the people and allowed them to trade it to meet their quota.

sentences.zh: 知連州。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗將朝謁太清宮，選通判亳州。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was about to attend the Grand Pure Palace, he was selected as vice prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong was to attend the Grand Pure Palace, Ruogu was selected as vice prefect of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷度支員外郎、權三司戶部判官，出為京東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to outer aide of the Revenue Section and acting judge of the Household Section of the Three Departments, then went out as transport commissioner of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to outer aide of the Revenue Section and acting judge of the Household Section of the Three Departments, then was sent out as transport commissioner of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 會河決白馬，調取芻楗，同列盧士倫協三司意，趣刻擾州縣，而若谷寬之。

translations.literal: When the river broke at Baima, fodder and timbers were levied; his colleague Lu Shilun cooperated with the Three Departments' intent and urged harsh pressure on prefectures and counties, while Ruogu was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke at Baima and fodder and timbers were levied, his colleague Lu Shilun cooperated with the Three Departments and pressed the prefectures harshly, while Ruogu was lenient.

sentences.zh: 士倫不悅，構於朝，徙知陝州。

translations.literal: Shilun was displeased, framed him at court, and he was transferred to prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun was displeased, slandered him at court, and Ruogu was transferred to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盜聚青灰山久不散，遣牙吏持榜招諭之，盜殺其黨與自歸。

translations.literal: Bandits gathered at Qinghui Mountain and long would not disperse; he sent a clerk with a proclamation to summon them; the bandits killed their own associates and surrendered themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits had gathered at Qinghui Mountain for a long time; he sent a clerk with a proclamation to summon them, and the bandits killed several of their own men and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 改梓州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，判三司戶部勾院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, he judged the Audit Office of the Household Section of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiansheng era he served as administrator of the Audit Office of the Household Section of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，陛辭，不俟垂簾請對，乃遽詣長春殿奏事，罷知荊南。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, at his farewell audience he did not wait for the curtain to be drawn to request an audience but abruptly went to the Hall of Everlasting Spring to report affairs; he was dismissed from Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, at his farewell audience he did not wait for the regent to grant an audience but went straight to the Hall of Everlasting Spring to report; he was dismissed from Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 士族元甲恃蔭屢犯法，若谷杖之，曰：「吾代若父兄訓之爾。」

translations.literal: The gentry clansman Yuan Jia, relying on yin privilege, repeatedly violated the law; Ruogu caned him, saying: "I am disciplining you in place of your father and elder brothers."
translations.idiomatic: The gentry clansman Yuan Jia, relying on yin privilege, repeatedly broke the law; Ruogu had him caned, saying, "I am disciplining you in your father's place."

sentences.zh: 王蒙正為駐泊都監，挾太后姻橫肆，若谷繩以法。

translations.literal: Wang Mengzheng was garrison commander; relying on his connection to the empress dowager, he acted arrogantly; Ruogu bound him with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mengzheng was garrison commander and, relying on his tie to the empress dowager, acted arrogantly; Ruogu restrained him by law.

sentences.zh: 監司右蒙正，奏徙若谷潭州。

translations.literal: The supervisory officials favored Mengzheng and memorialized to transfer Ruogu to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisory officials sided with Mengzheng and had Ruogu transferred to Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洞庭賊數邀商人船，殺人輒投屍水中。

translations.literal: Bandits on Dongting repeatedly waylaid merchants' boats; when they killed people they at once cast the corpses into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits on Dongting Lake repeatedly waylaid merchant vessels; when they killed someone they threw the body into the water.

sentences.zh: 嘗捕獲，以屍無驗，每貸死，隸他州。

translations.literal: When they were once captured, because there was no corpse as evidence, they were each spared death and registered in other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When captured, the lack of a corpse as evidence meant they were usually spared execution and registered in other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 既而逃歸，復功劫，若谷擒致之，磔於市。

translations.literal: Having escaped and returned, they again plundered; Ruogu seized them and dismembered them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: After they escaped and returned to their raids, Ruogu captured them and had them dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 自是寇稍息。

translations.literal: From this the banditry gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After that the banditry gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿、集賢殿修撰、知滑州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, compiler of the Academy Hall, and prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, compiler of the Academy, and prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河齧韓村堤，夜馳往，督兵為大埽，至旦堤完。

translations.literal: The river gnawed the dike at Hancun; he galloped there by night and supervised troops in building a great embankment; by dawn the dike was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the river breached the dike at Hancun, he rode there by night, supervised troops in building a great embankment, and by dawn the dike was restored.

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫知延州。

translations.literal: As Right Remonstrator he was made prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Remonstrator he was made prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州有東西兩城夾河，秋、夏水溢，岸輒圮，役費不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The prefecture had eastern and western cities flanking the river; in autumn and summer the water overflowed and the banks repeatedly collapsed; labor costs could not be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had eastern and western cities on either side of the river; in autumn and summer floods repeatedly collapsed the banks, at incalculable cost in labor.

sentences.zh: 若谷乃製石版為岸，押以巨木，後雖暴水，不復壞。

translations.literal: Ruogu then made stone slabs for the banks and pinned them with great timbers; afterward, even in violent floods, they were no longer destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu had stone slabs made for the banks and pinned them with great timbers; afterward, even in violent floods, the banks held.

sentences.zh: 官倉依山而貯穀少，若谷使作露囤，囤可貯二萬斛，他郡多取法焉。

translations.literal: The government granary, built against the mountain, stored little grain; Ruogu had open-air bins made; each bin could store twenty thousand hu; many other prefectures took this as a model.
translations.idiomatic: The government granary, built against a hillside, held little grain; Ruogu had open-air bins built that could store twenty thousand hu each, and many other prefectures followed his example.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、知壽州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor and made prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor and made prefect of Shou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 豪右多分占芍陂，陂皆美田，夏雨溢壞田，輒盜決。

translations.literal: Powerful families largely encroached on the Shao Marsh; the marsh lands were all fine fields; when summer rains overflowed and damaged fields, they would secretly breach the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families had largely encroached on Shao Marsh, whose shores were prime farmland; when summer rains flooded and damaged crops, they would secretly breach the dikes.

sentences.zh: 若谷摘冒占田者逐之，每決，輒調瀕陂諸豪，使塞堤，盜決乃止。

translations.literal: Ruogu singled out those who had encroached and expelled them; whenever there was a breach, he would summon the powerful families along the marsh to seal the dikes, and secret breaches then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu expelled those who had encroached illegally; whenever a breach occurred, he summoned the powerful families along the marsh to repair the dikes, and secret breaches ceased.

sentences.zh: 加集賢院學士、知江寧府。

translations.literal: He was made academician of the Academy and prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Academy and prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 卒挽舟過境，寒瘠甚者，留養視之，須春溫遣去。

translations.literal: Boat haulers passing through the territory who were severely cold and emaciated he retained to nourish and care for them, sending them away only when spring grew warm.
translations.idiomatic: Boat haulers passing through who were severely cold and emaciated he kept and cared for until spring warmth allowed them to go on.

sentences.zh: 民丐於道者，以分隸諸僧寺，助給舂爨。

translations.literal: Commoners begging along the roads he assigned in groups to various Buddhist temples to help provide pounding and cooking.
translations.idiomatic: Beggars along the roads he assigned to various Buddhist temples, which helped provide food and lodging.

sentences.zh: 還，勾當三班院，進龍圖閣直學士、知河南府。

translations.literal: On his return he managed the Three-Rank Court; he was advanced to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and made prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he managed the Three-Rank Court, was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and made prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 貴人多葬洛陽，敕使須索煩擾，若谷奏令鴻臚預約所調移府，逆為營辦。

translations.literal: Many nobles were buried at Luoyang; imperial envoys' demands were vexatious; Ruogu memorialized that the Court of Imperial Entertainments should arrange in advance what was to be requisitioned and transferred to the prefecture, preparing it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Many nobles were buried at Luoyang, and imperial envoys' demands were a constant nuisance; Ruogu memorialized that the Court of Imperial Entertainments should arrange requisitions in advance so the prefecture could prepare everything beforehand.

sentences.zh: 改樞密直學士、知并州。

translations.literal: He was changed to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and made prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民貧失婚姻者，若谷出私錢助其嫁娶。

translations.literal: Among the people, those too poor to marry, Ruogu paid from private funds to assist their weddings.
translations.idiomatic: For the poor who could not afford marriage, Ruogu paid from his own funds to help them wed.

sentences.zh: 贅婿、亡賴委妻去，為立期，不還，許更嫁。

translations.literal: When sons-in-law living in the household or wastrels abandoned their wives and left, he set a deadline; if they did not return, remarriage was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When wastrel sons-in-law abandoned their wives, he set a deadline; if they did not return, the women were allowed to remarry.

sentences.zh: 并多降人，喜盜竊，籍累犯者，以三人為保，有犯，並坐之，悛者削去籍名。

translations.literal: Bing had many surrendered peoples who delighted in theft; he registered repeat offenders, made groups of three guarantors; if one offended, all were punished together; those who reformed had their names struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had many surrendered peoples prone to theft; he registered repeat offenders and required groups of three as guarantors—if one offended, all were punished; those who reformed were struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 進尚書工部侍郎、龍圖閣直學士、知開封府，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Works in the Secretariat, direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture, and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and prefect of Kaifeng, and appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 建言：「風俗惡，媺在上之人作而新之。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When customs are bad, it is for those above to reform and renew them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "When customs are corrupt, it is for those in authority to reform and renew them.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，各有其類，今一目以朋黨，恐正人無以自立矣。」

translations.literal: Gentlemen and petty men each have their kind; now to label all alike as faction, I fear upright men will have no means to stand on their own."
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and petty men each have their kind; to label all alike as faction now will leave upright men no room to stand on their own."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，為下詔諭中外。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and issued an edict to instruct the inner and outer [realms].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and issued an edict to the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 以耳疾，累上章辭位，罷為資政殿大學士、吏部侍郎、提舉會靈觀事。

translations.literal: Because of ear ailment, he repeatedly memorialized to resign his post; he was dismissed to Grand Academician of the Hall of Assistance in Governance, Vice Minister of Personnel, and superintendent of Huiling Temple affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because of an ear ailment he repeatedly asked to resign; he was relieved as grand academician of the Hall of Assistance in Governance, vice minister of personnel, and superintendent of Huiling Temple.

sentences.zh: 以太子少傅致仕，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He retired as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; he died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as junior tutor to the crown prince and died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太傅，諡康靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, posthumous name Kangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor to the crown prince, with the posthumous name Kangjing (Peaceful and Serene).

sentences.zh: 若谷性資端重，在政府，論議常近寬厚。

translations.literal: Ruogu's nature and bearing were upright and weighty; in government his discourse tended toward lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu was upright and grave in character; in council his counsel tended toward lenience.

sentences.zh: 治民多智慮，愷悌愛人，其去，多見思。

translations.literal: Governing the people he employed much forethought, was kindly and loved others; when he left, many missed him.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people he was thoughtful and kindly; when he left office, many missed him.

sentences.zh: 少時與韓億為友，及貴顯，婚姻不絕焉。

translations.literal: In youth he was friends with Han Yi; when both rose to eminence, marriage ties between them never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was friends with Han Yi; once both had risen to eminence, marriage ties between their families never ceased.

sentences.zh: 子淑。

translations.literal: His son was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shu.

sentences.zh: 子 淑

translations.literal: Son: Shu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shu

sentences.zh: 淑，字獻臣，年十二，真宗幸亳，獻文行在所。

translations.literal: Shu, style name Xianchen, at age twelve when Zhenzong visited Bo, presented a literary work at the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Xianchen, at twelve when Emperor Zhenzong visited Bo, presented a literary work at the imperial encampment.

sentences.zh: 真宗奇之，命賦詩，賜童子出身。

translations.literal: Zhenzong marveled at him, ordered him to compose poetry, and granted him the degree of student-of-talent initiation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong was astonished, ordered him to compose a poem, and granted him the degree of student-of-talent initiation.

sentences.zh: 試秘書省校書郎，寇準薦之，授校書郎、館閣校勘。

translations.literal: He was examined for collator of the Secretariat; Kou Zhun recommended him, and he was appointed collator and Hanlin collation reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He was examined for collator of the Secretariat; Kou Zhun recommended him, and he was appointed collator and Hanlin collation reviewer.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，遷大理評事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing, he was transferred to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianxing era, he was transferred to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 修《真宗實錄》，為檢討官。

translations.literal: He compiled the Veritable Records of Zhenzong as an investigating compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Zhenzong as an investigating compiler.

sentences.zh: 書成，改光祿寺丞、集賢校理，為國史院編修官。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was made aide of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and collation reviewer of the Assembled Worthies Hall, and compiler in the Institute of National History.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he was made aide of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and collation reviewer of the Assembled Worthies Hall, and a compiler in the Institute of National History.

sentences.zh: 召試，賜進士及第，改秘書郎，進太常丞、直集賢院、同判太常寺，擢史館修撰，再遷尚書禮部員外郎，上時政十議。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination, granted jinshi with highest honors, changed to secretary; advanced to aide of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, direct academician of the Assembled Worthies Hall, and concurrent judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; promoted to historiographer of the History Office; again transferred to outer director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat; he submitted Ten Discourses on Current Policy.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for examination, he was granted jinshi with highest honors and made a secretary; he rose to aide of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, direct academician of the Assembled Worthies Hall, and concurrent judge of that court, was promoted to historiographer of the History Office, then to outer director of the Ministry of Rites, and submitted Ten Discourses on Current Policy.

sentences.zh: 改知制誥、勾當三班院，為翰林學士，進吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to drafter of edicts and superintendent of the Three-Rank Bureau, made Hanlin academician, and advanced to outer director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made drafter of edicts and superintendent of the Three-Rank Bureau, appointed Hanlin academician, and promoted to outer director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會若谷參知政事，改侍讀學士，加端明殿學士。

translations.literal: When Ruogu became Vice Grand Councilor, [Shu] was changed to attendant reader academician and added academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruogu became vice grand councilor, Shu was made attendant reader academician and also academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 若谷罷，進本曹郎中，典豫王府章奏。

translations.literal: When Ruogu was dismissed, [Shu] advanced to director of his own bureau and managed memorials of the Prince of Yu's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruogu left office, Shu was promoted to director of his bureau and managed memorials for the Prince of Yu's household.

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫知許州。

translations.literal: As Right Remonstrance Commissioner he was prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As right remonstrance commissioner he served as prefect of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，取民所食五種上之，帝惻然，為蠲其賦。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he presented the five kinds of food the people were eating; the emperor was moved to pity and remitted their taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he presented the five kinds of food the people were eating; the emperor was moved to pity and remitted their taxes.

sentences.zh: 權知開封府，復為翰林學士、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He acted as prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture, then again became Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as prefect of Kaifeng, then again became Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 言者指其在開封多褻近吏人，改給事中、知鄭州。

translations.literal: Critics said that in Kaifeng he was too familiar with clerks and attendants; he was changed to supervising editor and prefect of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that in Kaifeng he was improperly familiar with clerks and runners; he was made supervising editor and prefect of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙河陽，轉尚書禮部侍郎，復為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Heyang, promoted to Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat, and again made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Heyang, promoted to vice minister of rites, and again made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 罷端明殿學士，判流內銓，復加端明殿學士。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as academician of the Duanming Hall, judged internal circulation selection, and again added as academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed as academician of the Duanming Hall, placed in charge of internal circulation selection, and later restored as Duanming academician.

sentences.zh: 初，在鄭州，作《周陵詩》。

translations.literal: Earlier, while at Zheng Prefecture, he composed the "Zhou Tomb Poetry."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while at Zheng Prefecture, he composed the "Zhou Tomb Poetry."

sentences.zh: 國子博士陳求古以私隙訟其議訕朝廷，除龍圖閣學士，出知應天府。

translations.literal: Guozi Doctor Chen Qiugu, out of private grievance, sued him for remarks mocking the court; he was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and sent out as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guozi doctor Chen Qiugu, nursing a private grudge, accused him of mocking the court; he was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and sent out as prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 累表論辨，不報，乃請侍養。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to argue his case without response, then requested leave to attend and support [his parents].
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized in his own defense without reply, then asked for leave to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 明年，復端明、侍讀二學士，判太常寺。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to both Duanming and attendant reader academicians and judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was restored as Duanming and attendant reader academician and placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 父喪免官，終喪起復，再為翰林學士。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he was dismissed from office; when mourning ended he was reappointed and again made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning; when the mourning period ended he was reappointed and again made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 諫官包拯、吳奎等言淑性奸邪，又嘗請侍養父而不及其母，罷翰林學士，以端明、龍圖閣學士奉朝請。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Bao Zheng, Wu Kui, and others said Shu's nature was treacherous and wicked, and that he had once asked to attend his father in retirement but not his mother; he was dismissed as Hanlin academician and made Duanming and Dragon Diagram academicians on stipend attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Bao Zheng, Wu Kui, and others said Shu was treacherous by nature and had once asked to care for his father in retirement but not his mother; he was removed as Hanlin academician and made Duanming and Dragon Diagram academicians on stipend attendance.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，為端明、侍讀二學士。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was made both Duanming and attendant reader academicians.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning period ended, he was again made Duanming and attendant reader academician.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎，復為翰林學士，而御史中丞張昇等又論奏之，不拜，除兼龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, again made Hanlin academician, but Supervising Censor Zhang Sheng and others again memorialized against him; he did not accept the appointment and was made concurrent academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of revenue and again made Hanlin academician, but supervising censor Zhang Sheng and others attacked him again; he declined the appointment and was made concurrent academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 由是壹鬱不得志，出知河中府，暴感風眩，卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon deeply pent-up and unfulfilled, he was sent out as prefect of Hezhong Prefecture; suddenly stricken with dizzying wind ailment, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter deeply frustrated and unfulfilled, he was sent out as prefect of Hezhong; he was suddenly stricken with vertigo and died.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 淑警慧過人，博習諸書，詳練朝廷典故，凡有沿革，帝多諮訪。

translations.literal: Shu was exceptionally clever beyond others, broadly studied all books, and was well versed in court precedents; whenever there was a reform or change, the emperor often consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was exceptionally clever, widely read, and thoroughly versed in court precedent; whenever institutions changed, the emperor often consulted him.

sentences.zh: 制作誥命，為時所稱。

translations.literal: His drafting of edicts was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His drafting of edicts was praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 其他文多裁取古語，務為奇險，時人不許也。

translations.literal: His other writings mostly cut and took ancient phrases, striving for strangeness and peril; contemporaries did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: His other writings mostly culled archaic phrases and strove for strangeness and difficulty; contemporaries did not approve.

sentences.zh: 初，宋郊有學行，淑恐其先用，因密言曰：「『宋』，國姓；

translations.literal: Earlier, Song Jiao had learning and conduct; Shu feared he would be used first and therefore secretly said: "'Song' is the surname of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Song Jiao had learning and conduct, Shu feared Jiao would be promoted first and secretly said, "'Song' is the surname of the state;

sentences.zh: 而『郊』者交，非善應也。」

translations.literal: and 'jiao' means exchange—an inauspicious omen."
translations.idiomatic: and 'jiao' means 'exchange'—an inauspicious omen."

sentences.zh: 又宋祁作《張貴妃制》，故事，妃當冊命，祁疑進告身非是，以淑明典故問之，淑心知其誤，謂祁曰：「君第進，何疑邪？」

translations.literal: Also Song Qi drafted the edict for Consort Zhang; by precedent consorts were to receive investiture; Qi doubted that advancing the notification of appointment was improper and asked Shu, who knew precedents; Shu knew in his heart it was wrong but told Qi, "Sir, just advance it—why doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi also drafted the edict for Consort Zhang; by precedent a consort was to receive formal investiture, and Qi doubted that submitting the notification of appointment was correct, so he asked Shu, who knew court precedent. Shu knew it was wrong but told Qi, "Just submit it—why hesitate?"

sentences.zh: 祁遂得罪去，其傾側險陂類此。

translations.literal: Qi thereupon offended and left office; his partisan deviousness was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Qi thereupon gave offense and left office; his devious partisanship was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 嘗修《國朝會要》、《三朝訓鑒圖》、《閣門儀制》、《康定行軍賞罰格》，又獻《繫訓》三篇，所著別集百餘卷。

translations.literal: He once compiled the State Court Essentials, the Three Reigns Training Mirror, Gate Protocols, and the Kangding Military Rewards and Punishments Regulations; he also presented three memorials on the System of Instruction; his collected works numbered more than a hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the State Court Essentials, the Three Reigns Training Mirror, Gate Protocols, and the Kangding Military Rewards and Punishments Regulations; he also presented three essays on the System of Instruction; his collected works ran to more than a hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 子壽朋、復圭。

translations.literal: His sons were Shoupeng and Fugui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shoupeng and Fugui.

sentences.zh: 孫 壽朋

translations.literal: Grandson: Shoupeng
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shoupeng

sentences.zh: 壽朋，字延老。

translations.literal: Shoupeng, style name Yanlao.
translations.idiomatic: Shoupeng, courtesy name Yanlao.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，與弟復圭同試學士院，賜進士出身，判吏部南曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, he and his younger brother Fugui together were examined at the Hanlin Academy, granted jinshi initiation, and judged the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingli era, he and his younger brother Fugui were examined together at the Hanlin Academy, granted jinshi initiation, and appointed to judge the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 使行諸陵，奏言：「昭憲皇后誕育二聖，為國文母，獨以合葬安陵，不及時祭，請更其禮。」

translations.literal: Sent on tour of the imperial tombs, he memorialized: "Empress Zhao Xian bore the two sage emperors and was the civil mother of the state; she alone was buried with joint rites at Anling without timely sacrifices—I request that the ritual be changed."
translations.idiomatic: On a tour of the imperial tombs he memorialized, "Empress Zhao Xian bore the two sage emperors and was the civil mother of the state, yet she alone was buried at Anling without regular sacrifices—I ask that the rites be revised."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 遷群牧判官，擊斷敏甚。

translations.literal: He was transferred to reviewer of the Imperial Herds Office; his decisions were swift and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to reviewer of the Imperial Herds Office, where his decisions were swift and sharp.

sentences.zh: 皇城卒邏其縱遊無度，出知汝州。

translations.literal: Imperial City guards monitored his unrestrained travels; he was sent out as prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial City guards reported his unrestrained travels; he was sent out as prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盡推職田之入歸前守楊畋；

translations.literal: He turned over all income from office fields to the former prefect Yang Tian;
translations.idiomatic: He turned over all income from office fields to his predecessor Yang Tian;

sentences.zh: 畋死，又經理其家。

translations.literal: when Tian died, he again managed his household.
translations.idiomatic: when Tian died, he again managed his household affairs.

sentences.zh: 以饑歲，營州廨勞民，降為荊門軍。

translations.literal: In a famine year he requisitioned the people to work on the prefectural offices; he was demoted to Jingmen Army.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he pressed the people to work on the prefectural offices and was demoted to Jingmen Army.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官、戶部判官、知鳳翔府滄州。

translations.literal: He served as push official of Kaifeng Prefecture, revenue bureau judge, and prefect of Fengxiang Prefecture and Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as push official of Kaifeng, revenue bureau judge, and prefect of Fengxiang and Cang Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 滄地震，壞城郭帑庾。

translations.literal: Cang Prefecture had an earthquake that destroyed the walls and granaries.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake at Cang Prefecture destroyed the walls and granaries.

sentences.zh: 壽朋以席為屋，督吏寀繕葺，未數月，復其舊。

translations.literal: Shoupeng used mats for roofs, supervised clerks to gather materials and repair, and within months restored them to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: Shoupeng roofed buildings with mats, supervised clerks in gathering materials and repairs, and within months restored everything.

sentences.zh: 括蕪田三萬頃，縱民耕，擇其壯者使習兵。

translations.literal: He reclaimed thirty thousand qing of waste land, let the people farm it, and chose the strong among them to train in arms.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed thirty thousand qing of waste land, let the people farm it, and chose the able-bodied among them to train in arms.

sentences.zh: 河方北湧，隨塞之，故道狹，壽朋度必東潰，諭居人徙避，後三縣四鎮果墊焉。

translations.literal: The Yellow River was surging northward; he blocked it as it came, but the old channel was narrow; Shoupeng gauged that it would certainly burst eastward and urged residents to move away; later three counties and four towns were indeed inundated.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River was surging north; he blocked it as it came, but the old channel was narrow. Shoupeng judged it would burst eastward and urged residents to move; later three counties and four towns were indeed inundated.

sentences.zh: 司馬光出使，薦其能，加直史館。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang went on a mission he recommended his ability; [Shoupeng] was added as direct historiographer of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang went on a mission he recommended his ability, and Shoupeng was made direct historiographer of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 入直舍人院、同修起居注，進戶部、鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He entered the Drafting Academy on duty, concurrently recorded the emperor's acts, and was advanced to Vice Commissioner of Revenue and Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Drafting Academy on duty, served concurrently as recorder of the emperor's acts, and was promoted to vice commissioner of revenue and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 性疏雋任俠，奉祠西太一宮，飲酒食肉如常時，暴得疾卒。

translations.literal: His nature was free, lofty, and chivalrous; while holding sacrifice at the Western Supreme Unity Temple he ate meat and drank wine as in ordinary times, then suddenly took ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was free-spirited and chivalrous by nature; while holding sacrifice at the Western Supreme Unity Temple he ate and drank as usual, then was suddenly stricken and died.

sentences.zh: 詔中使撫其孥，賜白金三百兩。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a palace attendant to comfort his family and granted three hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a palace attendant to comfort his family and granted three hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 孫 復圭

translations.literal: Grandson: Fugui
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Fugui

sentences.zh: 復圭，字審言。

translations.literal: Fugui, style name Shenyan.
translations.idiomatic: Fugui, courtesy name Shenyan.

sentences.zh: 通判澶州。

translations.literal: He was concurrent prefect of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as concurrent prefect of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 北使道澶，民主驛率困憊。

translations.literal: Northern envoys passed through Duan; the prefecture master and postal stations were mostly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Northern envoys passed through Duan, and the prefect and postal stations were mostly worn out.

sentences.zh: 豪杜氏十八家，詭言唐相如晦後，每賕吏脫免，復圭按籍役之。

translations.literal: Eighteen great Du clans falsely claimed to be descendants of the Tang minister Du Xiangruhui; each bribed clerks to escape corvée; Fugui checked the registers and conscripted them.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen powerful Du clans falsely claimed descent from the Tang minister Du Xiangruhui and routinely bribed clerks to escape corvée; Fugui checked the registers and conscripted them.

sentences.zh: 知滑州。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兵匠相忿鬩，揮所執鐵椎，椎殺爭者於廳事，立斬之。

translations.literal: Artisan soldiers quarreled in mutual hatred; one swung the iron mallet he held and with it killed a disputant in the hall; [Fugui] immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Artisan soldiers quarreled; one swung the iron mallet he held and killed a disputant in the hall; Fugui had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 徙知相州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自太宗時，聚夏人降者五指揮，號「廳子馬」，子弟相承，百年無它役。

translations.literal: Since Taizong's time, surrendered Xia people had been gathered in five finger commands, called "hall-son horses," passed down from sons to younger brothers for a century without other service.
translations.idiomatic: Since Taizong's time, surrendered Xia people had been gathered in five finger commands called "hall-son horses," passed from sons to younger brothers for a century without other service.

sentences.zh: 復圭斥不如格者，選能騎射士補之。

translations.literal: Fugui expelled those not meeting standards and selected able archers and riders to fill the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Fugui expelled those who did not meet standards and selected able archers and riders to replace them.

sentences.zh: 為度支判官、知涇州。

translations.literal: He was revenue bureau judge and prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as revenue bureau judge and prefect of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始時二稅之入，三司移折已重，轉運使又覆折之，復圭為奏免，民立生祠。

translations.literal: At first the intake of the two-tax system was already heavily discounted by the Three Departments' transfers, and transport commissioners discounted it again; Fugui memorialized for exemption, and the people erected living shrines.
translations.idiomatic: At first the two-tax intake was already heavily discounted in Three Departments transfers, and transport commissioners discounted it again; Fugui memorialized for exemption, and the people erected living shrines to him.

sentences.zh: 歷湖北、兩浙、淮南、河東、陝西、成都六轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as transport commissioner of Hubei, Liang-Zhe, Huainan, Hedong, Shaanxi, and Chengdu—six circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner for six circuits: Hubei, Liang-Zhe, Huainan, Hedong, Shaanxi, and Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 浙民以給衙前役，多破產，復圭悉罷遣歸農，令出錢助長名人承募，民便之。

translations.literal: Zhe people, because of supplying yamen-runner service, often went bankrupt; Fugui dismissed them all back to farming and ordered them to pay money to help chief households take contracts; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe people were often ruined supplying yamen-runner corvée; Fugui dismissed them all back to farming and let them pay money to help leading households take contracts, which the people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 瀕海人賴蛤沙地以生，豪家量受稅於官而占為己有，復圭奏蠲其稅，分以予民。

translations.literal: Coastal people relied on clam-and-sand flats to live; great families collected tax for the government by measure and occupied them as their own; Fugui memorialized to remit the tax and divide the land among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal people lived on clam and sand flats; powerful families paid measured tax to the state and seized the land; Fugui memorialized to remit the tax and divide the flats among the people.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，進直龍圖閣、知慶州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, he was advanced to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era, he was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夏人築壘於其境，不犯漢地。

translations.literal: The Xia people built ramparts within their own territory and did not violate Han land.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia built fortifications within their own territory and did not violate Song territory.

sentences.zh: 復圭貪邊功，遣大將李信帥兵三千，授信以陳圖，使自荔原堡夜出襲擊，敗還，復圭斬信自解。

translations.literal: Fugui, greedy for border merit, sent the great general Li Xin to command three thousand troops, gave Xin a battle map, and had him sortie by night from Liyuan Fort to raid; defeated, he returned; Fugui beheaded Xin to absolve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for border glory, Fugui sent General Li Xin with three thousand men, gave him a battle plan, and ordered a night raid from Liyuan Fort; defeated, Xin returned, and Fugui beheaded him to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 又欲澡前恥，遣別將破其金湯、白豹、西和市，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: He also wished to wash away his previous shame and sent other generals to smash their Jintang, Baibao, and Xihe markets, taking several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing also to wash away his earlier shame, he sent other generals to smash Jintang, Baibao, and Xihe markets, taking several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 後七日，秉常舉國入寇。

translations.literal: Seven days later Bingchang led the whole nation in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later Li Bingchang led a full-scale invasion.

sentences.zh: 御史謝景溫劾復圭擅興，致士卒死傷，邊民流離，謫保靜軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Censor Xie Jingwen impeached Fugui for unauthorized initiation of war, causing soldiers to die and be wounded and border people to be displaced; he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xie Jingwen impeached Fugui for unauthorized warfare that killed and wounded soldiers and displaced border people; he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，知光化軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was prefect of Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made prefect of Guanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 張商英言：「夏人謀犯塞之日久矣，與破金湯適相值，非復圭生事。」

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying said: "The Xia people had long plotted to raid the border; breaking Jintang happened to coincide with that—it was not Fugui provoking trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shangying said, "The Xia had long been plotting a border raid; the attack on Jintang merely coincided with that—it was not Fugui who provoked the trouble."

sentences.zh: 乃召判吏部流內銓，知曹、蔡、滄州，還為鹽鐵副使，以集賢殿修撰知荊南，卒。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to judge internal circulation selection in the Ministry of Personnel, was prefect of Cao, Cai, and Cang Prefectures, returned as Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron, and as Academician of the Assembled Worthies Hall was prefect of Jingnan; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled to judge internal circulation selection in the Ministry of Personnel, served as prefect of Cao, Cai, and Cang Prefectures, returned as vice commissioner of salt and iron, and as academician of the Assembled Worthies Hall was prefect of Jingnan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 復圭臨事敏決，稱健吏，與人交不以利害避。

translations.literal: Fugui in affairs was quick and decisive, called a capable official; in dealings with others he did not avoid them for gain or harm.
translations.idiomatic: Fugui was quick and decisive in affairs and was called a capable official; in dealings with others he did not shun them for gain or loss.

sentences.zh: 然輕率躁急，無威重，喜以語侵人，獨為王安石所知，故既廢即起。

translations.literal: Yet he was rash and impatient, without dignified weight, and liked to insult people with words; only Wang Anshi understood him, so once dismissed he was soon reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rash and impatient, lacked dignified bearing, and liked to insult people verbally; only Wang Anshi valued him, so once dismissed he was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 王博文

translations.literal: Wang Bowen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bowen

sentences.zh: 王博文，字仲明，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Bowen, style name Zhongming, was a native of Jiyin in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bowen, courtesy name Zhongming, was a native of Jiyin in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖諫，給事太宗藩邸，為西京作坊副使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was an attendant in Taizong's princely residence and became vice commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian had served in Taizong's princely household and became vice commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 博文年十六，善屬文，舉進士開封府，以回文詩百篇為公卷，人謂之「王回文」。

translations.literal: Bowen at age sixteen was skilled at literary composition; he took the jinshi examination at Kaifeng Prefecture and used a hundred palindrome poems as his public portfolio; people called him "Wang Palindrome."
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Bowen was skilled at composition; he took the jinshi examination at Kaifeng and submitted a hundred palindrome poems as his public portfolio, earning the nickname "Wang Palindrome."

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，太宗親試進士，以年少罷歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, Taizong personally examined jinshi candidates; because [Bowen] was young, he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua, Taizong personally examined jinshi candidates; because Bowen was young, he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 後諫卒官廬州，州守劉蒙叟為言，召試舍人院，為安豐主簿，歷南豐尉，有能名。

translations.literal: Later Jian died in office at Lu Prefecture; the prefect Liu Mengsou spoke on [Bowen's] behalf; he was summoned to test at the Drafting Academy, made registrar of Anfeng, and served as warden of Nanfeng—he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jian died in office at Lu Prefecture; the prefect Liu Mengsou spoke for him; Bowen was summoned to test at the Drafting Academy, made registrar of Anfeng, and served as warden of Nanfeng, earning a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 調南劍州軍事推官，改大理寺丞，監荊南榷貨務，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military judicial officer of Nanjian Prefecture, changed to aide of the Court of Judicial Review, supervised the Jingnan monopoly bureau, and was promoted to palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military judicial officer of Nanjian, made aide of the Court of Judicial Review, supervised the Jingnan monopoly bureau, and was promoted to palace aide.

sentences.zh: 陳堯諮薦之，試中書，賜進士第，擢知濠州，歷真州。

translations.literal: Chen Yaozi recommended him; he was examined at the Secretariat, granted the jinshi degree, appointed prefect of Hao Prefecture, and served at Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yaozi recommended him; he was examined at the Secretariat, granted the jinshi degree, appointed prefect of Hao Prefecture, and later served at Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸亳，權江淮制置司事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong visited Bo, [Bowen] acted as commissioner of the Huai-Hai Circuit Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong visited Bo, he acted as commissioner of the Huai-Hai circuit commission.

sentences.zh: 改監察御史、梓州路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was changed to investigating censor and transport commissioner of the Zizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor and transport commissioner of the Zizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 以疾，請出知海州，徙密州。

translations.literal: Because of illness he requested a post outside the capital as prefect of Hai Prefecture and was transferred to Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he asked for an outside post as prefect of Hai Prefecture and was transferred to Mi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 負海有鹽場，歲饑，民多盜鬻，吏捕之輒抵死。

translations.literal: Along the coast there were salt works; in a year of famine many people stole and sold [salt]; whenever officials arrested them they were punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Along the coast there were salt works; when famine struck, many people stole salt to sell, and officials who arrested them invariably sent them to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 博文請弛鹽禁，候歲豐乃復，從之。

translations.literal: Bowen requested relaxation of the salt prohibition, to be restored when the year was abundant; [the court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen asked that the salt monopoly be eased until the harvest improved; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a palace censor in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，朱能、王先在長安偽為《乾祐天書》，事覺，能既敗死，先與其徒就禽，詔博文乘驛按劾。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era Zhu Neng and Wang Xian in Chang'an falsely made the "Qianyou Heavenly Book"; when the affair was exposed Neng had already been defeated and died; Xian and his followers were captured; [the emperor] ordered Bowen to go by express courier to investigate and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi years Zhu Neng and Wang Xian forged a "Qianyou Heavenly Book" at Chang'an. When the plot was exposed Neng had already been defeated and killed; Xian and his followers were seized. Bowen was ordered to travel by express post to investigate and prosecute the case.

sentences.zh: 博文唯治首惡，脅從者七人，得以減論。

translations.literal: Bowen punished only the chief culprits; seven coerced followers received reduced sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen prosecuted only the ringleaders; seven coerced followers received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 還為開封府判官，丁母憂。

translations.literal: He returned [to the capital] as judge of Kaifeng Prefecture and entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as a judge of Kaifeng Prefecture and then went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 始，博文幼喪父，其母張氏改適韓氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning Bowen had lost his father young; his mother Lady Zhang remarried into the Han clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen had lost his father in childhood; his mother, née Zhang, had remarried into the Han family.

sentences.zh: 及博文在朝，謂子無絕母禮，請得以恩封之。

translations.literal: When Bowen was at court he said a son has no ritual of severing from a mother and requested that he be granted favor enfeoffment for her.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bowen held court office, he held that no son may formally sever ties with his mother and asked that she be ennobled through his own favor.

sentences.zh: 母死，又謂古之為父後者不為出母服，以廢宗廟祭也。

translations.literal: When his mother died he also said that in antiquity one who succeeded as heir to the father's line did not wear mourning for an "outgoing" mother, in order to avoid abolishing ancestral temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, he further argued that in antiquity an heir who had succeeded his father's line did not mourn an estranged mother, lest ancestral sacrifices be neglected.

sentences.zh: 今喪者皆祭，無害於行服。

translations.literal: Now those in mourning all sacrifice; there is no harm in performing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In his day mourners still performed sacrifices, he said, so observing mourning would not interfere with rites.

sentences.zh: 乃請解官持服，然議者以喪而祭為非禮。

translations.literal: He then requested to resign office and observe mourning, yet critics held that sacrificing while in mourning was contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign and observe the mourning period, but critics held that conducting sacrifices during mourning was unorthodox.

sentences.zh: 服除，為三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became revenue judge of the State Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was made revenue judge of the State Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 出為河北轉運使，遷侍御史、陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: He went out as transport commissioner of Hebei, was promoted to attendant censor and transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Hebei transport commissioner, then promoted to attendant censor and Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 屬羌撒逋渴以族落數千帳叛，既又寇原州柳泉鎮、環州鵓鴿泉砦，梧州刺史杜澄、內殿崇班趙世隆戰沒。

translations.literal: At this time the Qiang Sa'bo Ke rebelled with several thousand tents of his tribe; he then also raided Liuchuan town in Yuan Prefecture and the Bogu Spring stockade in Huan Prefecture; Prefect Du Cheng of Wu Prefecture and Inner Hall Duty Officer Zhao Shilong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Qiang leader Sa'bo Ke rebelled with several thousand clan tents. He raided Liuchuan in Yuan Prefecture and the Bogu Spring stockade in Huan Prefecture; Du Cheng, prefect of Wu, and Inner Hall officer Zhao Shilong were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 博文劾奏內侍都知周文質、押班王懷信為涇原、環慶兩路鈐轄，提重兵駐大拔砦，玩寇逗留，耗用邊費，請用曹瑋、田敏代。

translations.literal: Bowen impeached Inner Service Director Zhou Wenzhi and Escort Commissioner Wang Huaixin as controllers of the Jingyuan and Huanqing circuits, who held heavy troops stationed at Daba stockade, dallied with the enemy and delayed, wasting border funds; he requested Cao Wei and Tian Min to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen memorialized against Inner Service director Zhou Wenzhi and escort commissioner Wang Huaixin, joint controllers of the Jingyuan and Huanqing circuits, who kept a large force at Daba stockade yet dallied with the enemy and wasted frontier funds. He asked that Cao Wei and Tian Min replace them.

sentences.zh: 既而文質、懷信坐法，遂以瑋知永興軍，使節制邊事。

translations.literal: Soon Wenzhi and Huaixin were punished by law; then Wei was made prefect of Yongxing Army and commissioned to control border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi and Huaixin were soon punished by law; Wei was appointed prefect of Yongxing and given overall charge of frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 會瑋病不行，又用敏為涇原路總管，寇遂平。

translations.literal: But Wei fell ill and could not go; Tian Min was then used as overall commander of Jingyuan Circuit and the raiders were soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fell ill and could not take up the post; Min was made overall commander of Jingyuan, and the raids subsided.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書兵部員外郎，為三司戶部副使，再遷戶部郎中、龍圖閣待制、判吏部流內銓、權發遣三司使事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat, became vice commissioner of the revenue department of the State Finance Commission, then again promoted to director of the revenue department, Dragon Diagram Hall attendant academician, judged the Personnel Registry, and acted as commissioner of State Finance affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of War, made vice commissioner of the State Finance revenue department, then advanced to revenue director, Dragon Diagram attendant academician, registrar of the Personnel Registry, and acting commissioner of the State Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 與監察御史崔暨、內侍羅崇勳同鞫真定府曹汭獄。

translations.literal: Together with investigating censor Cui Ji and inner attendant Luo Chongxun he jointly tried the case of Cao Rui of Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Together with investigating censor Cui Ji and inner attendant Luo Chongxun he jointly investigated the Cao Rui case in Zhending Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及還，權知開封府，進龍圖閣直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: Upon return he acted as prefect of Kaifeng, was advanced to Dragon Diagram Hall direct academician and prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he acted as prefect of Kaifeng, then was promoted to Dragon Diagram direct academician and made prefect of Qin.

sentences.zh: 為走馬承受賈德昌所毀，徙鳳翔府，又徙永興軍。

translations.literal: He was slandered by mobile imperial inspector Jia Dechang, transferred to Fengxiang Prefecture, then again transferred to Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Slandered by mobile inspector Jia Dechang, he was transferred to Fengxiang and then to Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 明年，德昌以贓敗，改樞密直學士，復知秦州。

translations.literal: The next year Dechang was ruined for corruption; [Bowen] was changed to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and again made prefect of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Dechang was brought down on corruption charges; Bowen was made a direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and restored to Qin.

sentences.zh: 初，沿邊軍民之逃者必為熟戶畜牧，又或以遺遠羌易羊馬，故常沒者數百人。

translations.literal: At first along the border fleeing soldiers and civilians were invariably taken in by affiliated tribal households for herding, or also given away to distant Qiang in exchange for sheep and horses; thus those regularly lost numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly fugitives from the border armies and populace were routinely sheltered by affiliated tribal households as herdsmen, or traded off to distant Qiang for sheep and horses, so several hundred people were regularly lost.

sentences.zh: 其禽生羌，則以錦袍、銀帶、茶絹賞之。

translations.literal: When they captured raw Qiang they rewarded them with brocade robes, silver belts, tea, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Those who captured unsubdued Qiang were rewarded with brocade robes, silver belts, tea, and silk.

sentences.zh: 間有自歸，而中道為夏人所得，亦不能辨，坐法皆斬。

translations.literal: Occasionally some returned of themselves, but en route were taken by Xia people and could not be distinguished; by law all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Some tried to return on their own, but if Tanguts seized them en route they could not be distinguished from enemies and were beheaded under the law.

sentences.zh: 博文乃遣習知邊事者，密持信紙往招，至則悉貸其罪，由是歲減殊死甚眾。

translations.literal: Bowen then sent those skilled in border affairs to go secretly bearing letters to recruit; when they arrived he entirely pardoned their offenses; thereby each year capital crimes were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen sent men skilled in frontier affairs to carry letters of assurance in secret; when fugitives arrived he pardoned them all. Thereafter executions for capital offenses fell sharply year by year.

sentences.zh: 朝廷下其法旁路。

translations.literal: The court issued his method to neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The court extended his policy to neighboring frontier circuits.

sentences.zh: 又言河西回鶻多緣互市家秦、隴間，請悉遣出境，戒守臣使譏察之。

translations.literal: He also said many Hexi Uyghurs relied on border-market households in Qin and Long; he requested that all be sent outside the borders and warned defending officials to inspect and scrutinize.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that many Hexi Uighurs were lodging with border traders in Qin and Long and asked that they all be sent beyond the frontier, with local officials ordered to watch and intercept them.

sentences.zh: 再遷右諫議大夫，以龍圖閣學士復知開封府。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to right remonstrance official and as Dragon Diagram academician again acted as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to right remonstrance official and, as a Dragon Diagram academician, again took charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 都城豪右邸舍侵通衢，博文製表木按籍，命左右判官分徹之，月餘畢。

translations.literal: In the capital powerful families' mansions encroached on thoroughfares; Bowen made tally posts according to the register and ordered the left and right judges to divide and demolish them; in a little over a month it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the mansions of powerful families encroached on the main roads. Bowen set up marker posts from the registry and ordered his deputy judges to clear them section by section; the work was finished in a little over a month.

sentences.zh: 出知大名府，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Daming Prefecture and was promoted to presenting academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Daming and promoted to presenting academician.

sentences.zh: 召權三司使，遂同知樞密院事，逾月而卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned to act as commissioner of the State Finance Commission, then jointly managed Bureau of Military Affairs affairs; after a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to act as finance commissioner and then as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; a month later he died.

sentences.zh: 帝臨奠，贈尚書吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor attended his funeral offering; he was posthumously granted vice director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him and posthumously made him vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 博文以吏事進，多任劇繁，為政務平恕，常語諸子曰：「吾平生決罪，至流刑，未嘗不陰擇善水土處，汝曹志之。」

translations.literal: Bowen advanced through clerical affairs, often held heavy and complicated posts, and in governing was balanced and forbearing; he often told his sons: "Throughout my life in sentencing crimes, down to exile punishments, I have never failed privately to choose a place of good soil and water; you should remember this."
translations.idiomatic: Bowen had risen through administrative service and often held demanding posts; in office he was evenhanded and lenient. He often told his sons, "Whenever I passed sentence, even to exile, I always chose in private a place with good land and water. Remember that."

sentences.zh: 然治曹汭獄，議者多謂博文希太后旨，縱崇勳傅致其罪。

translations.literal: Yet in trying the Cao Rui case, many in discussion said Bowen curried the empress dowager's intent and indulged Chongxun in fabricating his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Cao Rui trial many said Bowen had courted the empress dowager's favor and let Chongxun manufacture charges against him.

sentences.zh: 子疇。

translations.literal: His son was Chou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chou.

sentences.zh: 子 疇

translations.literal: Son: Chou
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chou

sentences.zh: 疇，字景彝，以父蔭補將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Chou, style name Jingyi, entered office by his father's privilege as principal clerk of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chou, courtesy name Jingyi, entered office through his father's privilege as principal clerk of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and through accumulation was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士宋祁提舉諸司庫務，薦疇勾當公事。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Song Qi supervised various warehouse bureaus and recommended Chou to manage official business.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Song Qi, who oversaw the various warehouse bureaus, recommended Chou to handle their affairs.

sentences.zh: 時有宦官同提舉者，疇辭於中書曰：「翰林先進，疇恐不得事也。

translations.literal: At the time there was a eunuch who jointly supervised; Chou declined at the Secretariat saying: "The Hanlin [academician] comes first; I fear I would not be able to serve.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch was appointed joint supervisor. Chou declined at the Secretariat, saying, "The Hanlin academician takes precedence; I fear I could not be of use.

sentences.zh: 然以朝士大夫而為閹人指使，則疇實恥之。」

translations.literal: Yet for a court scholar-official to be directed by a eunuch—then Chou would truly be shamed."
translations.idiomatic: But for a court scholar-official to take orders from a eunuch—that, Chou said, he would truly find shameful."

sentences.zh: 用賈昌朝薦，改編修《唐書》。

translations.literal: By Jia Changchao's recommendation he was changed to compile and edit the Book of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On Jia Changchao's recommendation he was reassigned to help compile the Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 仁宗獵近郊，疇引十事以諫。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong hunted in the near suburbs; Chou cited ten matters to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong hunted near the capital, Chou offered ten points of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，手詔禁貴戚近習私謁者，疇獻《聖政惟公頌》。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era an imperial handwritten edict forbade noble kin and close attendants from private visits; Chou presented "An Ode to Sagely Governance and Solely Fairness."
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, after an imperial autograph forbade private audiences by noble kin and intimates, Chou presented "An Ode to Sagely Governance and Sole Fairness."

sentences.zh: 召試，直秘閣，為開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to examination, made directly attached to the Secret Repository, and became investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed a summons examination, was made a direct attache of the Secret Repository, and appointed investigating officer of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 宦者李允良訴其叔父死，疑為仇家所毒，請發棺驗視，眾欲許之，疇獨不可。
