translations.literal: Eunuch Li Yunliang sued that his uncle had died, suspected poison by an enemy house, and requested opening the coffin for examination; the multitude wanted to permit it—only Chou objected.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Yunliang claimed his uncle had died, suspecting enemy kin of poisoning him, and asked to open the coffin for examination. Most officials were ready to agree; Chou alone refused.

sentences.zh: 曰：「苟無實，是無故而暴屍，且安知非允良有奸？」

translations.literal: He said: "If there is no evidence, this is wantonly exposing a corpse without cause—and who knows whether Yunliang himself has ulterior intent?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Without evidence this would mean exposing a corpse for no reason—and how do we know the accuser himself has no ulterior motive?"

sentences.zh: 窮治，果與其叔父家有怨。

translations.literal: Through exhaustive investigation it turned out he indeed bore a grudge against his uncle's household.
translations.idiomatic: A full investigation showed he did indeed hold a grudge against his uncle's family.

sentences.zh: 歷三司度支判官、修起居注、知制誥、權判吏部流內銓，以右諫議大夫權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He served as expenditure judge of the State Finance Commission, edited the Diarist, drafted edicts, acted as judge of the Personnel Registry, and as right remonstrance official acted as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as expenditure judge of the finance commission, edited the Veritable Records, drafted edicts, acted as registrar of the Personnel Registry, and as right remonstrance official served as acting vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時陳升之拜樞密副使，諫官、御史唐介等奏彈升之不當大用，朝廷持不行，介等爭數月不已，乃兩罷之。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Shengzhi was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; remonstrance officials and censors such as Tang Jie memorialized impeaching that Shengzhi should not be greatly employed; the court held and did not act; Jie and others disputed for months without end; then both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shengzhi was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, remonstrators and censors including Tang Jie memorialized that he was unfit for high office. The court held the appointment in abeyance; Jie and others protested for months until both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而論者謂介等為眾人遊談所誤。

translations.literal: Yet commentators said Jie and others were misled by the idle talk of the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators, however, said Jie and his allies had been led astray by rumor-mongers.

sentences.zh: 疇疏言：「浮華險薄之徒，往來諫官、御史家，掎摭人罪，寖以成俗，請出詔戒勵。」

translations.literal: Chou memorialized: "Flamboyant, frivolous, and treacherous persons come and go to the homes of remonstrance officials and censors, picking at people's faults, gradually making it custom—please issue an edict to warn and encourage."
translations.idiomatic: Chou memorialized, "Frivolous and vicious men haunt the homes of remonstrators and censors, picking at people's faults until it has become custom. I ask that an edict be issued to warn and correct this."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to presenting academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to presenting academician.

sentences.zh: 英宗既即位，感疾，皇太后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yingzong had ascended he contracted illness; the empress dowager drew the curtain and listened to government.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yingzong took the throne he fell ill, and the empress dowager ruled from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 其後帝疾平，猶未御正殿，疇上疏請御朝聽政。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor's illness abated but he still did not attend the main hall; Chou submitted a memorial requesting he hold court and hear government.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered he still did not attend court in the main hall; Chou memorialized asking him to preside and hear affairs.

sentences.zh: 及永昭陵復土，祭仁宗虞主於集英殿，以宗正卿攝事。

translations.literal: When Yongzhao Mausoleum was re-covered with earth, he sacrificed to Renzong's spirit tablet at Jiying Hall, with the Director of the Imperial Clan acting as proxy.
translations.idiomatic: When earth was returned at Yongzhao Mausoleum, the spirit tablet of Renzong was honored with a yu sacrifice in Jiying Hall, with the director of the imperial clan presiding on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 疇奏曰：「人子之葬其親，送形而往，迎神而返，故虞祭所以安神也。

translations.literal: Chou memorialized: "When a son buries his parent he sends the form away and welcomes the spirit back; therefore the yu sacrifice is to settle the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Chou submitted, "When a son buries his parent he sends the body forth and welcomes the spirit home; the yu sacrifice exists to settle the spirit.

sentences.zh: 位尊者禮重，禮重者祭多，故天子之虞數至於九。

translations.literal: The loftier the station the heavier the ritual; the heavier the ritual the more sacrifices—thus the Son of Heaven's yu rites reach nine in number.
translations.idiomatic: The loftier the rank, the weightier the rites—and the weightier the rites, the more sacrifices—so a Son of Heaven may perform as many as nine yu rites.

sentences.zh: 今山陵，嗣君不得親往，則道路五虞，理可命宗正攝事。

translations.literal: Now at the mountain tomb the heir cannot go in person; then the five yu rites along the road—reasonably the Director of the Imperial Clan may be ordered to act as proxy.
translations.idiomatic: At the mausoleum today the heir cannot go in person; the five yu rites along the route may reasonably be entrusted to the director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 若神主既至，則四虞之祭，雖或聖躬未寧，亦宜勉彊。

translations.literal: If the spirit tablet has already arrived, then the four yu sacrifices—even if the sacred person is not yet at ease—should still be undertaken with effort.
translations.idiomatic: Once the spirit tablet has arrived, the four remaining yu sacrifices ought to be performed even if Your Majesty's health is still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 況陛下在藩邸，以好古知禮、仁孝聰明聞於中外，此先帝所以託天下也。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty in the princely residence was known within and without for loving antiquity, knowing ritual, benevolence, filial piety, and intelligence—this is why the late emperor entrusted the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In your princely days you were renowned within and without for learning antiquity, mastering ritual, and filial wisdom—this is why the late emperor entrusted you with All under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣願始終令德，以全美名。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes you to maintain excellent virtue from beginning to end, to perfect your fine name."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that you preserve this excellence to the end and perfect your good name."

sentences.zh: 帝既視朝前後殿，而於聽事猶持謙抑。

translations.literal: The emperor had already attended court in the front and rear halls, yet in hearing affairs still maintained modest restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had begun holding court in the front and rear halls, yet in conducting affairs he remained markedly modest and reserved.

sentences.zh: 疇復上疏曰：「廟社擁佑陛下，起居安平，臨朝以時，僅逾半載，而未聞開發聽斷，德音遏塞，人情缺然。

translations.literal: Chou again submitted a memorial, saying: "The altars of state and land protect Your Majesty; your rising and resting are peaceful; you attend court on time—barely more than half a year has passed—yet we have not heard you open and develop in hearing and deciding; virtuous pronouncements are blocked; popular feeling is wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Chou submitted another memorial: "The altars of state protect Your Majesty; you rise and rest in peace and attend court on schedule—yet in more than half a year we have not heard you open deliberation and decide affairs. Your gracious words are stifled and the people's hearts are left wanting.

sentences.zh: 伏望思太祖、太宗艱難取天下之勞，真宗、仁宗憂勤守太平之力，勉於聽決大政，以慰母后之慈。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will reflect on Taizu and Taizong's toil in the hardship of taking the realm, and Zhenzong and Renzong's anxious diligence in guarding peace; strive in hearing and deciding great affairs, to comfort the empress dowager's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to recall the toil of Taizu and Taizong in winning the realm through hardship, and the anxious diligence of Zhenzong and Renzong in keeping the peace; exert yourself in deciding great affairs of state, to comfort the empress dowager's loving heart.

sentences.zh: 勿為疑貳謙抑，自使盛德闇然不光。」

translations.literal: Do not through doubt and excessive modest restraint yourself make your great virtue dim and unbright."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let doubt and excessive modesty dim the brightness of your great virtue."

sentences.zh: 未幾，又上疏曰：

translations.literal: Before long he again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「董仲舒為武帝言天人之際曰：『事在勉彊而已。

translations.literal: "Dong Zhongshu told Emperor Wu on the relation of Heaven and man: 'The matter lies in striving—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: "Dong Zhongshu told Emperor Wu of the relation between Heaven and man: 'The matter lies in striving—that is all.

sentences.zh: 勉彊學問，則聞見廣而智益明；

translations.literal: Strive in learning and inquiry, then what is heard and seen broadens and wisdom grows clearer;
translations.idiomatic: Strive in learning and inquiry, and what you hear and see will broaden while your wisdom grows clearer;

sentences.zh: 勉彊行道，則德日起而大有功』，陛下起自列邸，光有天命，然而祖宗基業之重，天人顧享之際，所以操心治身、正家保國者，尤在於勉強力行也。

translations.literal: strive in practicing the Way, then virtue rises day by day and great achievement is made'—Your Majesty rose from the ranks of princely residences, bright with Heaven's mandate; yet the weight of the ancestral foundation, the moment when Heaven and man look to enjoy blessings—for minding the heart, governing the person, rectifying the family, and guarding the state—lies especially in striving and forceful action.
translations.idiomatic: strive in practicing the Way, and virtue will rise day by day until great deeds are achieved.' Your Majesty rose from the ranks of princes, radiant with Heaven's mandate; yet given the weight of the ancestral foundation and the moment when Heaven and man look to you for blessing, the care of heart and person, the ordering of family and state, depend above all on striving and resolute action.

sentences.zh: 陛下昔在宗藩，已能務德好學，語言舉動未嘗越禮，是天性有聖賢之資。

translations.literal: Your Majesty formerly in the imperial clan princedom was already able to pursue virtue and love learning; in speech and conduct you never overstepped ritual—this is nature endowed with the capacity of sages.
translations.idiomatic: In your days in the imperial clan you already pursued virtue and loved learning; in speech and conduct you never overstepped ritual—your nature bears the makings of a sage.

sentences.zh: 自疾平以來，於茲半歲，而臨朝高拱，無所可否。

translations.literal: Since your illness abated, half a year has passed, yet at court you sit with hands folded high, affirming or denying nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Since your recovery half a year has passed, yet at court you sit with folded hands, affirming or denying nothing.

sentences.zh: 群臣關白軍國之政者日益至，其請人主裁決者日益多，然猶聖心盤桓，無所是非者，何也？

translations.literal: Ministers reporting on military and state affairs daily increase; those requesting the sovereign's judgment daily multiply—yet still the sacred heart hesitates, affirming or denying nothing—why?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers reporting on military and civil affairs grow more numerous by the day; petitions for your judgment multiply—yet your sacred heart still hesitates, deciding nothing. Why?

sentences.zh: 得非以初繼大統，或慮未究朝廷之事，故謙抑而未皇耶？

translations.literal: Could it be that having newly succeeded to the great succession, you perhaps fear you have not yet mastered court affairs, and therefore are modest and not at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Is it because you have newly succeeded to the throne and fear you have not yet mastered court affairs, and so hold back out of modesty?

sentences.zh: 或者聖躬尚未寧，而不欲自煩耶？

translations.literal: Or perhaps the sacred person is not yet at ease and does not wish to trouble yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Or is Your Majesty's health still unsettled and you do not wish to burden yourself?

sentences.zh: 抑有所畏忌而不言耶？

translations.literal: Or is there something you fear and avoid and do not speak of?
translations.idiomatic: Or is there something you fear and therefore hold back from speaking?

sentences.zh: 苟為謙抑而未皇，則國家萬務，日曠月廢，其勢將趨於禍亂無疑也。

translations.literal: If through modest restraint you are not at ease, then the myriad affairs of state daily lie idle and monthly waste away; the momentum will trend toward calamity and disorder without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If modest restraint keeps you from acting, the myriad affairs of state will daily lie idle and monthly waste away, and the momentum will surely trend toward calamity and disorder.

sentences.zh: 若聖躬未能寧，則天下之名醫良工，日可召於前。

translations.literal: If the sacred person is not yet at ease, then the realm's famous physicians and skilled craftsmen may daily be summoned before you.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's health is still unsettled, the realm's finest physicians and healers may be summoned before you every day.

sentences.zh: 而方技不試，藥石不進，養疾於身，坐俟歲月，非求全之道也。

translations.literal: Yet arts of healing are not tried, medicines and stones are not applied; you nurse illness in the person and sit awaiting the months—this is not the way to seek wholeness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no healing arts are tried and no medicines applied; to nurse illness in the body and sit awaiting time is not the way to seek full recovery.

sentences.zh: 苟有所畏忌而不言，則又過計之甚也。

translations.literal: If there is something you fear and avoid and do not speak of, then again this is excessive calculation.
translations.idiomatic: If you hold back from speaking out of fear, that is excessive caution indeed.

sentences.zh: 今中外之事，無可疑畏，臣嘗為陛下力言之矣。

translations.literal: Now affairs within and without—there is nothing doubtful to fear; your servant has already spoken forcefully to Your Majesty on this.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is nothing within or without the court that warrants such fear; I have already spoken to Your Majesty on this at length.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不坦心布誠、廓開大明以照天下，外則與執政大臣講求治體，內則於母后請所未至。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not open the heart and spread sincerity, broaden great brightness to illumine the realm—outwardly discuss with chief ministers the governing system, inwardly ask the empress dowager what has not yet been reached?
translations.idiomatic: Why not open your heart in sincerity and let great clarity shine upon the realm—outwardly discuss the principles of governance with chief ministers, inwardly ask the empress dowager what you have not yet understood?

sentences.zh: 延禮賢俊，諮訪忠直，廣所未見，達所未聞。

translations.literal: Extend courtesy to worthy and eminent men, consult loyal and upright ones, broaden what has not been seen, reach what has not been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Honor worthy men, consult the loyal and upright, broaden what you have not seen and reach what you have not heard.

sentences.zh: 若陛下朝行之，則眾心夕安矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty acts on this in the morning, then the multitude's hearts will be at peace by evening.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty acts on this in the morning, the people's hearts will be at peace by evening.

sentences.zh: 況陛下向居藩邸，日夕於側者，惟一二講學之師，與左右給使之人耳。

translations.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty formerly dwelt in the princely residence, those at your side day and night were only one or two teachers of learning and attendants at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When you lived in the princely residence, those at your side day and night were only one or two tutors and a handful of attendants.

sentences.zh: 修身行己，德業日新，而知者無幾，則是為善多而得名常少也；

translations.literal: Cultivating the person and practicing conduct, virtue and achievement daily renewed, yet those who knew were few—thus doing good was much while fame was often little;
translations.idiomatic: You cultivated yourself and your virtue grew day by day, yet few knew of it—doing much good while winning little renown;

sentences.zh: 然而終能德成行尊，美名遠聞，此先帝之所以屬心也。

translations.literal: yet in the end you were able to have virtue complete and conduct honored, fine name heard far—this is why the late emperor set his heart on you.
translations.idiomatic: yet in the end your virtue was complete and your conduct honored, your fine name heard far and wide—this is why the late emperor set his heart on you.

sentences.zh: 今處億兆之上，有一言動則天下知之，簡冊書之，比之於昔，是善行易顯而美名易成也。

translations.literal: Now you stand above the hundred millions; one word or act and the realm knows it, the bamboo slips record it—compared with the past, good conduct is easy to display and fine name easy to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Now you stand above the hundred millions; every word and act is known to the realm and recorded in the annals—compared with the past, good deeds are easy to display and a fine name easy to achieve.

sentences.zh: 然而尚莫之聞者，是不為爾，非不能也。

translations.literal: Yet still nothing is heard of this—not because you cannot, but because you do not act.
translations.idiomatic: Yet still nothing is heard of this—not because you cannot, but because you do not act.

sentences.zh: 有始有終者，聖賢之能事，在陛下勉彊而已。」

translations.literal: Having a beginning and an end—this is what sages and worthies can accomplish; it lies in Your Majesty's striving—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: To see a matter through from beginning to end is the mark of sages and worthies; it lies in Your Majesty's striving—that is all."

sentences.zh: 疇又上疏欲車駕行幸，以安人心。

translations.literal: Chou again submitted a memorial wishing the imperial carriage to travel on tour, to settle people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chou submitted another memorial asking that the emperor travel in state to reassure the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 時大臣亦有請，帝乃出禱雨，都人瞻望歡呼。

translations.literal: At the time great ministers also requested it; the emperor then went out to pray for rain; capital people gazed up and cheered.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers had also urged it; the emperor then went out to pray for rain, and the people of the capital looked on and cheered.

sentences.zh: 數日，皇太后還政，疇又上疏：「請詔二府大臣講求所以尊崇母后之禮。

translations.literal: Several days later the empress dowager returned government; Chou again submitted a memorial: "Please order the two offices' great ministers to discuss and seek the rites by which to honor the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the empress dowager returned the regency; Chou submitted another memorial: "I ask that the chief ministers of the two councils be ordered to devise rites for honoring the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷嚴奉之體，與歲時朔望之儀，車服承衛之等威，百司拱擬之制度，它時尊稱之美號，外家延賞之恩典，凡可以稱奉親之意者，皆宜優異章大，以發揚母后之功烈，則孝德昭於天下矣。」

translations.literal: If the court's body of solemn service, the rites of seasonal new and full moons, the graded majesty of carriages, robes, escort and guard, the regulations for which all offices bow and draft, the fine titles of honor at a later time, the favoring grants to the maternal kin—all that can express the intent of serving a parent—should all be exceptionally elevated and magnified, to display the empress dowager's achievements and merit, then filial virtue will shine upon the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Whether in the court's solemn observances, the rites of the seasons and new and full moons, the majesty of carriages, robes, escort and guard, the regulations drafted by all offices, future honorific titles, or favors for the maternal kin—all that can express devotion to a parent should be made exceptionally grand, to display the empress dowager's achievements, and filial virtue will shine throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 時詔近臣議仁宗配祭。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered close ministers to discuss Renzong's associated sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court ordered close ministers to debate Renzong's associated sacrifice at the altars.

sentences.zh: 故事，冬、夏至，祀昊天上帝、皇地祇，以太祖配；

translations.literal: By precedent, at winter and summer solstice they sacrificed to August Heaven and August Earth, with Taizu as associate;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, at the winter and summer solstices August Heaven and August Earth were sacrificed to, with Taizu as associate;

sentences.zh: 正月上辛祈穀，孟夏雩祀，孟冬祀神州地祇，以太宗配；

translations.literal: on the first xin day of the first month the prayer for grain, in the first month of summer the rain prayer, in the first month of winter sacrifice to the Spirit Land of the Divine Continent, with Taizong as associate;
translations.idiomatic: on the first xin day of the first month the prayer for grain, in early summer the rain sacrifice, in early winter sacrifice to the Spirit Land of the Divine Continent, with Taizong as associate;

sentences.zh: 正月上辛祀感生帝，以宣祖配；

translations.literal: on the first xin day of the first month sacrifice to the Emperor of Felt Life, with Xuanzu as associate;
translations.idiomatic: on the first xin day of the first month sacrifice to the Emperor of Felt Life, with Xuanzu as associate;

sentences.zh: 季秋大饗明堂、祀昊天上帝，以真宗配。

translations.literal: In late autumn there was the great feast at the Bright Hall, sacrificing to August Heaven, with Zhenzong as associate.
translations.idiomatic: In late autumn the court held the great feast at the Bright Hall, sacrificing to August Heaven with Emperor Zhenzong as associate.

sentences.zh: 而學士王珪等與禮官上議，以謂季秋大饗，宜以仁宗配，為嚴父之道。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Academician Wang Gui and others together with ritual officials submitted a proposal, holding that at the late-autumn great feast Renzong should serve as associate, in keeping with the rite of honoring one's stern father.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Academician Wang Gui and the ritual officials submitted a proposal holding that at the late-autumn great feast Renzong should serve as associate, in keeping with the rite of honoring one's stern father.

sentences.zh: 知制誥錢公輔獨謂仁宗不當配祭。

translations.literal: Document Drafting Commissioner Qian Gongfu alone held that Renzong should not serve as associated sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Document drafting commissioner Qian Gongfu alone held that Renzong should not serve as associated sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 疇以謂珪等議遺真宗不得配，公輔議遺宣祖、真宗、仁宗俱不得配，於禮意未安。

translations.literal: Chou held that Gui's proposal left Zhenzong without an associate, while Gongfu's would leave Xuanzu, Zhenzong, and Renzong all without associates—neither sat well with ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chou held that Gui's proposal would leave Zhenzong without an associate, while Gongfu's would leave Xuanzu, Zhenzong, and Renzong all without associates—neither sat well with ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 乃獻議曰：「請依王珪等議，奉仁宗配饗明堂，以符《大易》配考之說、《孝經》嚴父之禮。

translations.literal: He then submitted a proposal: "I ask that we follow Wang Gui and the others, installing Renzong as associate at the Bright Hall feast, in accord with the Classic of Changes' pairing with the father and the Classic of Filial Piety's rite of the stern father.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a proposal: "I ask that we follow Wang Gui and the others, installing Renzong as associate at the Bright Hall feast, in accord with the Classic of Changes' pairing with the father and the Classic of Filial Piety's rite of the stern father.

sentences.zh: 奉遷真宗配孟夏雩祀，以仿唐貞觀、顯慶故事。

translations.literal: Transfer Zhenzong to serve as associate at the early-summer rain sacrifice, following the Tang precedents of Zhenguan and Xianqing.
translations.idiomatic: Transfer Zhenzong to serve as associate at the early-summer rain sacrifice, following the Tang precedents of Zhenguan and Xianqing.

sentences.zh: 太宗依舊配正月上辛祈穀、孟冬祀神州祇，餘依本朝故事。

translations.literal: Let Taizong continue as associate at the first-xin-day prayer for grain in the first month and the early-winter sacrifice to the Spirit Land of the Divine Continent; let the rest follow our dynasty's precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Let Taizong continue as associate at the first-xin-day prayer for grain in the first month and the early-winter sacrifice to the Spirit Land of the Divine Continent; let the rest follow our dynasty's precedents.

sentences.zh: 如此，則列聖並侑；

translations.literal: Thus all the successive emperors would share the altar;
translations.idiomatic: Thus all the successive emperors would share the altar;

sentences.zh: 對越昊穹，厚澤流光，垂裕萬祀。

translations.literal: facing August Heaven, generous blessings flowing forth, abundant grace for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: facing August Heaven, with generous blessings flowing forth and abundant grace for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 必如公輔之議，則陷四聖為失禮，導陛下為不孝，違經戾古，莫此為甚。」

translations.literal: If we must follow Gongfu's proposal, we would cast the four sage emperors into breach of ritual, lead Your Majesty into unfilial conduct, and violate the classics and ancient practice—nothing could be worse."
translations.idiomatic: If we must follow Gongfu's proposal, we would cast the four sage emperors into breach of ritual, lead Your Majesty into unfilial conduct, and violate the classics and ancient practice—nothing could be worse."

sentences.zh: 自此公輔不悅，而朝廷以疇論事有補，帝與執政大臣皆器異之。

translations.literal: From this Gongfu was displeased, but the court regarded Chou's arguments as useful; the emperor and the chief ministers all held him in exceptional regard.
translations.idiomatic: From this Gongfu was displeased, but the court regarded Chou's arguments as useful; the emperor and the chief ministers all held him in exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士、尚書禮部侍郎、同提舉諸司庫務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Rites, and joint supervisor of the various warehouse bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Rites, and joint supervisor of the various warehouse bureaus.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: Several months later he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是公輔言疇望輕資淺，在臺素餐，不可大用，又頗薦引近臣可為輔弼者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gongfu said Chou's reputation was slight and his seniority shallow, that at the censorate he had eaten salary without work and was unfit for great appointment, and he also recommended several close ministers who might serve as chief counselors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gongfu said Chou's reputation was slight and his seniority shallow, that at the censorate he had drawn salary without earning it and was unfit for high office, and he also recommended several close ministers who might serve as chief counselors.

sentences.zh: 公輔坐貶。

translations.literal: Gongfu was demoted for it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu was demoted for it.

sentences.zh: 疇在位五十五日，卒。

translations.literal: Chou held office fifty-five days and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chou held office fifty-five days and died.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悼惜之，臨哭，賜白金三千兩，贈兵部尚書，諡「忠簡」。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him deeply, came in person to weep, granted three thousand taels of white silver, posthumously appointed him Minister of War, and gave the posthumous title "Loyal and Simple."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, came in person to weep, granted three thousand taels of white silver, posthumously appointed him Minister of War, and gave the posthumous title "Loyal and Simple."

sentences.zh: 疇名臣子，性介特，厲風操，喜言朝廷事。

translations.literal: Chou was the son of a renowned minister; by nature upright and unyielding, strict in conduct, fond of speaking on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was the son of a renowned minister; by nature upright and unyielding, strict in conduct, and fond of speaking on court affairs.

sentences.zh: 好治容服，坐立嶷然，言必文，未嘗慢戲，吏治審密，文辭嚴麗。

translations.literal: He cared for his dress and appearance, sat and stood with imposing bearing, always spoke in polished language, never engaged in coarse jesting, administered affairs with tight precision, and wrote in a strict, elegant style.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his dress and appearance, sat and stood with imposing bearing, always spoke in polished language, never engaged in coarse jesting, administered affairs with tight precision, and wrote in a strict, elegant style.

sentences.zh: 其執政未久、終於位及所享壽，類其父云。

translations.literal: His brief tenure in power, his death in office, and the span of years he enjoyed were all like his father's, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His brief tenure in power, his death in office, and the span of years he enjoyed were all like his father's, it is said.

sentences.zh: 王鬷，字總之，趙州臨城人。

translations.literal: Wang Zong, style name Zongzhi, was a native of Lincheng in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zong, courtesy name Zongzhi, was a native of Lincheng in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪父，哀毀過人。

translations.literal: At seven he lost his father and mourned with grief beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he lost his father and mourned with a grief beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 既長，狀貌奇偉。

translations.literal: When grown his form and bearing were singularly imposing.
translations.idiomatic: When grown his form and bearing were singularly imposing.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授婺州觀察推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating and prosecuting officer of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating and prosecuting officer of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代還，真宗見而異之，特遷秘書省著作佐郎、知祁縣，通判湖州。

translations.literal: When he returned from his term, Zhenzong saw him and was struck; he was specially promoted to Assistant Secretary in the Secretariat for Compilation, made magistrate of Qi County, and vice prefect of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his term, Emperor Zhenzong saw him and was struck; he was specially promoted to assistant secretary in the Secretariat for Compilation, made magistrate of Qi County, and vice prefect of Hu.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士、提點梓州路刑獄，權三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Judicial Intendant of the Zizhou Circuit, and acting Revenue Section Judge of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, judicial intendant of the Zizhou Circuit, and acting revenue-section judge of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 使契丹還，判都磨勘司。

translations.literal: After his mission to the Khitan he was made controller of the Directorate of Merit Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: After his mission to the Khitan he was made controller of the Directorate of Merit Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 以尚書度支員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Revenue Section of the Secretariat while also holding the post of Censor-in-Chief of Miscellaneous Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the revenue section of the Secretariat while also holding the post of censor-in-chief of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 上言：「方調兵塞決河，而近郡災歉，民力雕敝，請罷土木之不急者。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Troops are being mobilized to block the breached Yellow River, yet nearby prefectures suffer drought and famine and the people's strength is exhausted. I ask that non-urgent construction be halted."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Troops are being mobilized to block the breached Yellow River, yet nearby prefectures suffer drought and famine and the people's strength is exhausted. I ask that non-urgent construction be halted."

sentences.zh: 改三司戶部副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the revenue section.

sentences.zh: 樞密使曹利用得罪，鬷以同里為利用所厚，出知湖州，徙蘇州。

translations.literal: When Bureau Commissioner Cao Liyong fell from favor, Zong, being a fellow townsman whom Liyong had favored, was sent out as prefect of Hu and then transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bureau commissioner Cao Liyong fell from favor, Zong, being a fellow townsman whom Liyong had favored, was sent out as prefect of Hu and then transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 還為三司鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: On his return he became Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 時龍圖閣待制馬季良方用事，建言京師賈人常以賤價居茶鹽交引，請官置務收市之。

translations.literal: At the time Ma Jiliang of the Dragon Diagram Hall was in power and proposed that capital merchants often held tea-and-salt exchange notes at low prices; he asked that the state establish offices to buy them up.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ma Jiliang of the Dragon Diagram Hall was in power and proposed that capital merchants often held tea-and-salt exchange notes at low prices; he asked that the state establish offices to buy them up.

sentences.zh: 季良挾章獻姻家，眾莫敢迕其意，鬷獨不可，曰：「與民競利，豈國體耶！」

translations.literal: Jiliang relied on kinship with Empress Dowager Zhangxian; none dared oppose him, but Zong alone refused, saying, "To compete with the people for profit—what kind of state conduct is that!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiliang relied on kinship with Empress Dowager Zhangxian; none dared oppose him, but Zong alone refused, saying, "To compete with the people for profit—what kind of state conduct is that!"

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、判大理寺、提舉在京諸司庫務，安撫淮南，權判吏部流內銓，累遷刑部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, judge of the Court of Judicial Review, supervisor of capital warehouse bureaus, pacification commissioner of Huainan, acting director of the Ministry of Personnel's roster office, and rose through the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, judge of the Court of Judicial Review, supervisor of capital warehouse bureaus, pacification commissioner of Huainan, acting director of the Ministry of Personnel's roster office, and rose through the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 益、利路旱饑，為安撫使，以左司郎中、樞密直學士知益州。

translations.literal: When the Yi and Li circuits suffered drought and famine, he served as pacification commissioner, with the titles of Left Division Director and Academician Ex Officio of the Bureau of Military Affairs, governing Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yi and Li circuits suffered drought and famine, he served as pacification commissioner, with the titles of left division director and academician ex officio of the Bureau of Military Affairs, governing Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戍卒有夜焚營、殺馬、脅軍校為亂者，鬷潛遣兵環營，下令曰：「不亂者斂手出門，無所問。」

translations.literal: Some garrison soldiers by night burned the camp, killed horses, and coerced officers into mutiny; Zong secretly sent troops to surround the camp and ordered: "Those who did not join the mutiny, fold your hands and come out the gate—you will not be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Some garrison soldiers burned the camp by night, killed horses, and coerced officers into mutiny; Zong secretly sent troops to surround the camp and ordered: "Those who did not join the mutiny, fold your hands and come out the gate—you will not be questioned."

sentences.zh: 於是眾皆出，命軍校指亂者，得十餘人，即戮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all came out; he ordered the officers to point out the mutineers, seized more than ten men, and executed them at once.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all came out; he ordered the officers to point out the mutineers, seized more than ten men, and executed them at once.

sentences.zh: 及旦，人莫知也。

translations.literal: By dawn no one knew what had happened.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn no one knew what had happened.

sentences.zh: 其為政有大體，不為苛察，蜀人愛之。

translations.literal: His governance grasped the great pattern and avoided petty scrutiny; the people of Shu loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His governance grasped the great pattern and avoided petty scrutiny; the people of Shu loved him.

sentences.zh: 拜右諫議大夫、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrator and Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right remonstrator and associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 景祐五年，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingyou he became Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingyou he became vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷尚書工部侍郎、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，鬷嘗使河北，過真定，見曹瑋，謂曰：「君異日當柄用，願留意邊防。」

translations.literal: During Tiansheng, Zong had been sent to Hebei; passing through Zhending he met Cao Wei and said to him: "You will one day wield great power—please keep the frontier defenses in mind."
translations.idiomatic: During Tiansheng, Zong had been sent to Hebei; passing through Zhending he met Cao Wei and said to him: "You will one day wield great power—please keep the frontier defenses in mind."

sentences.zh: 鬷曰：「何以教之？」

translations.literal: Zong said, "What would you teach me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong said, "What would you teach me?"

sentences.zh: 瑋曰：「吾聞趙德明嘗使人以馬榷易漢物，不如意，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Wei said, "I have heard that Zhao Deming once sent men to trade horses at the frontier market for Han goods; when the bargain displeased him he wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "I have heard that Zhao Deming once sent men to trade horses at the frontier market for Han goods; when the bargain displeased him he wished to kill them.

sentences.zh: 少子元昊方十餘歲，諫曰：『我戎人，本從事鞍馬，而以資鄰國易不急之物，已非策，又從而斬之，失眾心矣。』

translations.literal: His younger son Yuanhao was just over ten and remonstrated: 'We Rong people live by saddle and horse; to spend our substance trading with a neighboring state for things we do not urgently need is already poor policy, and to kill men for it besides would lose the people's hearts.'
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Yuanhao was just over ten and remonstrated: 'We Rong people live by saddle and horse; to spend our substance trading with a neighboring state for things we do not urgently need is already poor policy, and to kill men for it besides would lose the people's hearts.'

sentences.zh: 德明從之。

translations.literal: Deming followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Deming followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 吾嘗使人覘元昊，狀貌異常，他日必為邊患。」

translations.literal: I once sent men to observe Yuanhao; his form and bearing were extraordinary—one day he will surely become a frontier menace."
translations.idiomatic: I once sent men to observe Yuanhao; his form and bearing were extraordinary—one day he will surely become a frontier menace."

sentences.zh: 鬷殊未以為然也。

translations.literal: Zong was far from convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was far from convinced.

sentences.zh: 比再入樞密，元昊反，帝數問邊事，鬷不能對。

translations.literal: When he again entered the Bureau of Military Affairs, Yuanhao rebelled; the emperor repeatedly asked about frontier affairs, and Zong could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When he again entered the Bureau of Military Affairs, Yuanhao rebelled; the emperor repeatedly asked about frontier affairs, and Zong could not answer.

sentences.zh: 及西征失利，議刺鄉兵，又久未決。

translations.literal: When the western campaign met defeat, the court debated tattooing militia recruits, and for a long time could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: When the western campaign met defeat, the court debated tattooing militia recruits, and for a long time could not decide.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，鬷與陳執中、張觀同日罷，鬷出知河南府，始歎瑋之明識。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Zong, Chen Zhizhong, and Zhang Guan were dismissed on the same day; Zong was sent out as prefect of Henan, and only then sighed over Wei's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry; Zong, Chen Zhizhong, and Zhang Guan were dismissed on the same day; Zong was sent out as prefect of Henan, and only then sighed over Wei's foresight.

sentences.zh: 未幾，得暴疾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he took a sudden illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took a sudden illness and died.

sentences.zh: 贈戶部尚書，諡忠穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of the Household and given the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of the Household and given the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 鬷少時，館禮部尚書王化基之門，樞密副使宋湜見而以女妻之。

translations.literal: In youth Zong lodged in the household of Minister of Rites Wang Huaji; Vice Bureau Commissioner Song Shen saw him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zong lodged in the household of Minister of Rites Wang Huaji; Vice Bureau commissioner Song Shen saw him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 宋氏親族或侮易之，化基曰：「後三十年，鬷富貴矣。」

translations.literal: Some of the Song clan's kin would slight him; Huaji said, "In thirty years Zong will be rich and honored."
translations.idiomatic: Some of the Song clan's kin would slight him; Huaji said, "In thirty years Zong will be rich and honored."

sentences.zh: 果如所言。

translations.literal: It came to pass as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It came to pass as he said.

sentences.zh: 論曰：吳育剛毅不撓，而設施無聞，其才不逮志者與？

translations.literal: Commentary: Wu Yu was firm and unyielding, yet his accomplishments went unheard—was his talent unequal to his ambitions?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Wu Yu was firm and unyielding, yet his accomplishments went unheard—was his talent unequal to his ambitions?

sentences.zh: 宋綬博洽明敏，若谷務長厚，博文習吏事，當仁宗時，先後與政，僅能恭慎寡過，保有祿位，施及後嗣。

translations.literal: Song Shou was broadly learned and keen, Ruogu devoted himself to forbearance and generosity, Bowen mastered administrative affairs; under Renzong they successively held power, managing only to be respectful and cautious with few faults, preserving their stipends and extending benefit to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shou was broadly learned and keen, Ruogu devoted himself to forbearance and generosity, Bowen mastered administrative affairs; under Renzong they successively held power, managing only to be respectful and cautious with few faults, preserving their stipends and extending benefit to their descendants.

sentences.zh: 敏求、淑俱練達典故，傅以文采，而淑以傾險敗德，視疇之介特，數建忠謀，則賢不肖之相去遠矣。

translations.literal: Minqiu and Shu were both versed in court precedents and adorned with literary grace, yet Shu ruined his virtue through treacherous conduct; compared with Chou's upright character and his repeated loyal counsels, the distance between the worthy and the unworthy could hardly be greater.
translations.idiomatic: Minqiu and Shu were both versed in court precedents and adorned with literary grace, yet Shu ruined his virtue through treacherous conduct; compared with Chou's upright character and his repeated loyal counsels, the distance between the worthy and the unworthy could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 王鬷不留意曹瑋之言，卒以昧於邊事見黜，宜哉！

translations.literal: Wang Zong paid no heed to Cao Wei's words and was finally dismissed for his ignorance of frontier affairs—as he deserved!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zong paid no heed to Cao Wei's words and was finally dismissed for his ignorance of frontier affairs—as he deserved!
